Recent findings suggest that we are introducing Stitch Loop, a product agent that connects to your codebase and live metrics to continuously optimize your software. It identifies issues, suggests fixes, and opens pull requests to help your team maintain product quality around the clock. You can join the waitlist today at stitch.google.com/loop/waitlist to get started with these automated tools for security, latency, and accessibility.

In a recent development, we are introducing Stitch Loop, a upcoming tool from Google Labs that helps you maintain and improve your software after it introduces. It connects to your code and live data to find bugs, fix security concerns, and boost performance around the clock. You simply review the suggested changes before they go live. This helps your team focus on building new features while the agent handles the ongoing work of keeping your product running well.

In a recent development, coding agents let you build and ship fresh features fast, but their job ends the moment your pull request merges. Once code hits production, the real work starts: patching vulnerabilities, speeding up checkout, and diagnosing signup drop-offs buried in noisy feedback. For lean teams, balancing post-launch maintenance with continuous improvement is a constant challenge, yet it’s also what drives some of the world’s most successful products.

Today, we are introducing Stitch Loop, a long-running product agent from Google Labs that connects to your codebase and live metrics, finds what needs fixing, and keeps working 24/7 on your product until your goals are met.

Millions of designers, developers, and founders already use Stitch to turn ideas into working interfaces in minutes. Together, Stitch and Stitch Loop are steps toward our broader ambition for Stitch: creating agents to help lean teams tackle the hardest parts of creating great products from ideation through continuous optimization.

It has been revealed that you start by connecting GitHub and your product context (logs, user behavior, feedback, etc) with over 180 integrations, custom MCP servers, or local CLI uploads. Grounded in that context, Stitch Loop runs evergreen loops to continuously optimize toward the measurable outcomes you care about. You get three default loops out of the box and can add your own anytime. Each loop runs through four steps:.

You always have the final call. Nothing merges until you review the PR.

Stitch Loop comes with built-in loops for cybersecurity, latency, and accessibility, plus the ability to create custom loops like improving checkout conversion.

Security is often the hardest gap to cover for lean teams shipping rapidly. Stitch Loop includes a dedicated security loop that pairs Gemini 4 Carbon's cyber security capabilities with CodeMender, Google DeepMind's autonomous agent that improves code security. Together, they scan your codebase for security vulnerabilities before they become incidents. Stitch Loop flags each issue it finds with evidence and opens a PR with a proposed fix for your review.

You can use Stitch Loop as a service layer for coding agents, like Google Antigravity, or bring it into the places where your team already works, like Slack.

Whatever coding agent you prefer can pull persistent product context from Stitch Loop via the Stitch CLI and MCP to power mixed-model setups and fully autonomous improvements in your existing workflow.

In Slack, just use @stitch to get daily insight digests and create newly introduced loops.

The Stitch Loop waitlist opens today for all consumers, globally, with eligible Google AI Ultra users getting priority access. Join at stitch.google.com/loop/waitlist and share your feedback in the Google Labs Discord.

Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

In a recent development, retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

Sources indicate that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

In a recent development, agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it's hard to believe that Spotify Wrapped is about to give us all a brutal reality check on how we soundtracked 2026. Though the idea of it sends shivers through me, it's still one of the most anticipated and exciting events on the tech calendar.

In a recent development, if you thought it was too late to get in your final listening hours, fear not; Spotify hasn't stopped counting them yet. While we don't know when the exact cut-off is (Spotify's never disclosed it before, and the likelihood of it happening is slim), it's widely thought to be right up until the launch of Wrapped, which usually lands in late November or early December.

The good news is that we still have between two and three weeks left before that day arrives, so if there was ever a good time to crack down on the final Wrapped preparations, it's now!

Recent findings suggest that for years, your Spotify Taste Profile has been sitting behind the algorithm, using your listening behaviors to determine which latest music it recommends to you. While you can exclude individual songs and playlists from infiltrating your Taste Profile, that's pretty much it as far as controlling how Spotify understands you.

Thankfully, the platform brought Taste Profile to the forefront of the experience earlier this year, allowing you to see exactly how Spotify understands your listening habits and how it uses this to shape your recommendations, and to flag any mistakes it makes. Not only that, but you can also speak directly to it and actively shape what it feeds you.

Using text prompts, you can ask your Taste Profile pretty much anything. If you want to explore a particular genre that's been on your list, you can prompt it to recommend more glam rock, experimental pop, or whatever you're feeling in the moment — and the same goes for artists.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

Industry observers note that if there's one thing that gets under my skin with music streaming apps is that, sometimes, you can run into artists you can't stand. No matter how much you try to ignore them, they're bound to crop up in your Discover Weekly or whenever you're listening to a Spotify-curated playlist — it's better to rid them completely, I say.

That's why I've gotten into the routine of blocking artists entirely from my feed. It's one of those features that, whenever I bring it up, others don't even know it exists. I'm here to tell you that it does, and it will change your life.

Industry observers note that all you need to do is head to an artist's page in the Spotify app, tap the three dots next to the 'Follow' button, and then select 'Don't play this artist'. Once that's enabled, their page will go gray, and their discography will disappear from playlists. Their music also won't show up in features like your Discover Weekly or Daylist, so your blocked artists won't get in the way of new music discovery.

Sources indicate that if you're on Spotify's Family plan and your young kids can't keep out of your profile, then I feel for you. There's nothing worse than waiting all year for Wrapped to arrive only to find that your top songs and artists are from your kids' favorite TV shows — the Family plan has individual profiles for a reason!

It's been difficult to avoid this in Wrapped's past, but rest assured Spotify has put its foot down on this infiltration this time around, and you can amend your settings to ensure this music stays far away from your Wrapped summary.

In your settings, you'll find a toggle that, when enabled, excludes all kids and family music that's played on your profile. Not only does this help with steering your Wrapped in a more accurate direction, but it also ensures that your kids' favorite music doesn't affect your recommendations, Discover Weekly, and Daily Mix — so it's not just a benefit for Wrapped.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eagles running back Saquon Barkley sold his equity stake in Polymarket after NFL rules barred players from holding prediction-market investments. The case sets the league apart from the NBA and MLB, which have signed deals with the exchanges, as the NFL argues at the Supreme Court that sports event contracts are gambling.

Saquon Barkley no longer owns a piece of Polymarket. The Eagles running back sold his equity stake to comply with league rules, he told Front Office Sports in an interview published October 28. It is the first public case of the NFL applying its gambling rules to a player’s prediction-market investment.

Barkley bought into Polymarket before the league told players they could not hold such investments. The NFL goes over endorsement, investment and training rules with players before every season.

The league has now made clear that its sportsbook restrictions extend to prediction markets. It declined to comment on Barkley’s case specifically. The stance was not latest to players. Kalshi and Polymarket were already off-limits to them as endorsers or brand ambassadors in January 2026. At that point, prediction markets were treated as gambling entities under the league’s gambling policy.

The NFL’s approach puts it at odds with other major leagues. Polymarket became Major League Baseball’s Official Prediction Market Exchange on March 19, 2026. On October 26, 2026, the NBA named both companies its preferred prediction-market exchanges. The agreement gives them rights to league intellectual property and marketing.

Sources indicate that NBA players face far lighter limits. They can hold stakes in the exchanges and appear in their marketing. The line is drawn only at promoting contracts on NBA games.

Industry observers note that the split also shuts NFL players out of an industry that leans heavily on their sport. By the league’s own figures, football made up $1.8 billion of prediction-market trading on the season’s first Sunday. That was more than half of the day’s total.

The league is pressing that view at the Supreme Court. On October 8, 2026, it filed an amicus brief supporting Newly introduced Jersey’s request for review in Flaherty v. KalshiEX, case No. 26-299. The NFL argued that sports prediction contracts are gambling. In its view, they are not financial swaps under exclusive federal oversight.

Fresh Jersey filed its petition on September 2, 2026. It followed an April ruling in which the Third Circuit sided 2-1 with Kalshi. The appeals court found that the CFTC has exclusive oversight of sports-event contracts.

Exclusive: Saquon Barkley tells FOS he was forced to divest his equity stake in Polymarket.

NFL players are not allowed to invest in or endorse gambling or prediction market companies.

— Front Office Sports (@FOS) October 28, 2026.

In a recent development, many of the NFL’s concerns will be addressed through the CFTC’s ongoing rulemaking, Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana said. In her view, the agency already has the power to police sports-related event contracts.

The Supreme Court granted Kalshi a 30-day extension to answer Latest Jersey. Its response, originally due October 8, must now be filed by November 9.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Storage can be a constant glitch if you're using a more budget-friendly or older device, but downloading the latest games doesn't mean you have to delete loads of pictures from your gallery or uninstall your favorite apps to create space.

That's because developer Level Infinite has just released a new version of PUBG Mobile designed specifically to be the lightest version of the popular battle royale game yet. The initial download of PUBG Mobile Flash takes up just 0.96GB, with multiple tools available to ensure subsequent content downloads are limited to the maps and modes you want to play – keeping as much free space on your phone as possible.

PUBG Mobile Flash also supports a wider range of devices than the base game, including those with just 2GB of RAM, and promises better graphics optimization for smoother frame rates.

The file size may be small, but Level Infinite makes it clear that this is still a fully fledged version of what it calls "one of the world’s most popular mobile games.".

PUBG Mobile Flash players will be able to squad up with their friends on regular PUBG Mobile. There is also seamless account cross-progression, so you'll be able to pick up where you left off if you already play the regular version of the game.

“Expanding access to PUBG Mobile has always been an notable part of our long-term vision, and we’re continually looking for new ways to connect players around the world,” explained general manager and PUBG Mobile head Vincent Wang.

"With PUBG Mobile Flash, we’re taking another step towards that goal, making it easier for more players to enjoy the core PUBG Mobile experience, reconnect with friends, and remain part of our global community.".

This new version of the game will likely prove popular in developing markets and among younger players where entry-level devices are common.

You can download it from the Google Play Store now.

You can also bring Gemini models into the session as you explore: it observes what is happening on screen, surfaces context-aware suggestion chips for where to go next, or triggers in-world events automatically as your journey unfolds.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple is kicking off a newly introduced and improved Health app next month with the release of iOS 27.3. Instead of just recording and displaying your health-related stats, the app will tap into Apple Intelligence to analyze the data and dispense advice on how to improve your health and fitness. But that reliance on AI means you’ll need the right type of iPhone to enjoy all the benefits.

Also: Apple could build its AI health chatbot from this study – how to enroll.

Here are five helpful new features built into the app, along with what you’ll need to access them.

In a recent development, first up, the app will offer suggestions based on data from different sources. For example, it might advise you to go for a walk at a nearby park if it detects that you’re not getting enough exercise. It may show you articles and videos about sleep if it finds that you’re not well-rested. It could also highlight possible conditions based on your lab and test results. You can easily view these recommendations from the Insights screen.

Also: Health is Tim Cook’s defining legacy – and your Apple Watch proves it.

Industry observers note that A newly introduced feature called Health Age compares your physical health to your actual age to show how you’re doing. The analysis draws on certain stats and lab data, such as your resting heart rate, sleep, heart rate variability (HRV), cholesterol, and A1C (average blood glucose levels), to deliver a health age, which may differ from your chronological age. The results can show you areas that may be of concern or that you need to focus on.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for.

With a new feature called Movement Evaluations and an iPhone and Apple Watch, the Health app can assess your flexibility, strength, balance, VO2 max (maximum oxygen absorption), and overall movement. You perform a physical routine while your iPhone “watches” you via the camera. Using built-in AI, the app will provide audio and visual feedback in real-time to tell you how you’re faring.

Apple promises that the analysis is performed on your device without recording, storing, or sharing the video.

Sources indicate that the upcoming app will be able to correlate your test results with data collected by your iPhone and Apple Watch to give you a more comprehensive picture of your health. Plus, Apple and Quest Diagnostics have teamed up to offer people in the US an optional $119 bloodwork panel that covers more than 50 biomarkers to scan for different health and medical conditions.

Also: I tested the Apple Watch Series 12 heart-rate claims against my gold-standard Polar strap.

Normally, you need an Apple Fitness+ subscription to fire up workout videos to help you exercise. But the new Health app will come with its own comprehensive set of training videos. Available from the Insights section, a series of strength exercise videos are designed to help you build your body strength. The videos cover all the key areas of your body to give you a full workout.

According to recent reports, some of the new features, such as the strength videos, will be available to all iPhone customers. But the ones that rely on AI will run only on phones that support Apple Intelligence. That means you’ll need an iPhone 15 Pro or Pro Max, any iPhone 16 or 17, an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, an iPhone Air, or an iPhone Duo.

#1623. Breaking: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool

📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Artex Is Criminals’ New Favorite ‘Point-and-Shoot’ AI Hacking Tool

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1182 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, over the past year, security researchers have warned that AI agents could vastly speed up cybercriminals’ ability to launch cyberattacks, breach companies, and ultimately steal money, data, or sensitive information from those compromised systems.
  • Recent findings suggest that since around the end of August, multiple companies, government agencies, and banks around the world have been targeted by cybercriminals adopting a latest wave of AI-powered penetration testing tools.
  • Sources indicate that dozens of these AI penetration frameworks or “harnesses,” which detail how an AI model should carry out cybersecurity testing or attacks, are increasingly being linked to real-world attacks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, over the past year, security researchers have warned that AI agents could vastly speed up cybercriminals’ ability to launch cyberattacks, breach companies, and ultimately steal money, data, or sensitive information from those compromised systems. For at least one subset of hackers, it appears that era has now arrived.

Recent findings suggest that since around the end of August, multiple companies, government agencies, and banks around the world have been targeted by cybercriminals adopting a latest wave of AI-powered penetration testing tools. These setups​​—many of which mimic legitimate defensive penetration testing techniques—use LLMs to autonomously scan potential hacking targets and attempt to force their way into poorly secured networks, then carry out attack plans written by human operators.

Sources indicate that dozens of these AI penetration frameworks or “harnesses,” which detail how an AI model should carry out cybersecurity testing or attacks, are increasingly being linked to real-world attacks. The tools do not introduce fresh ways to attack websites or servers and are not sophisticated, according to alerts from around half a dozen security companies. Instead, they allow cybercriminals to launch attacks at speeds that would be impossible for humans to do.

Sources indicate that hackers also don’t need to be skilled to use the tools, researchers say, and attacks that would have taken days are completed in just hours. “Agentic frameworks have progressed from experimental use to sustained, multi-objective offensive operations that run with minimal human intervention,” CJ Moses, AWS’s chief information security officer, wrote in a firm blog post recently.

Recent findings suggest that the most prominent of these tools is Artex. Written in the programming language Go, the open-source framework was first published on GitHub in July by a pseudonymous developer using the handle Autumn-27, and it’s been spreading across some hacker communities ever since. Artex has been used across all parts of attacks, from conducting initial analysis of networks and gaining access to moving within systems and preparing data to be exported.

“It’s really an all-in-one product,” indicates Jacob Larsen, an offensive security researcher and founder of security firm Cypen. “Previous iterations of AI agent pen-testing tools would either only do reconnaissance—like the scanning and analysis [of targets]—and some would only do testing. This is really a point-and-shoot weapon.”.

As with other AI hacking frameworks, Artex isn’t an AI product itself. Instead, it is essentially a guide that points external frontier and open-source AI models—that can be connected to it via APIs—to a series of existing penetration testing tools and processes. People using Artex or other similar setups can give simple, natural-language prompts to begin their operations. “Launch a penetration attack on [Redacted victim] to gain access to the site’s admin panel, database, or server,” one set of hackers prompted Artex, according to researchers at the security firm Check Point.

Once the instructions have been issued, multiple AI agents then carry them out. One agent will break down the plans into a series of tasks, others will try to perform these actions, and the system will then present its findings. Safety guardrails in the underlying AI models, particularly those from frontier labs, can stop hacking activity when they detect it. Increasingly, however, free Chinese and abliterated models are getting better at breaking into systems.

“It's fast; it’s efficient,” Guillaume Valadon, a researcher at security firm GitGuardian, states of Artex. Valadon and others say the simplicity of the tools makes it easier for unskilled wannabe hackers to try to enter the market—even if they have no clue about what they’re doing. “It lowers the bar,” Valadon says. “I would say my grandmother can do it, except that she doesn't have a laptop, but the bar is that low.”.

As a result, a flurry of reports from cybersecurity companies have linked Artex use to attempted and successful hacks—often by Chinese-speaking cybercriminals trying to make money. These include the theft of personal information from thousands of South Korean financial institutions, potential cryptocurrency theft, and hunting for exposed login details on GitHub.

“A variety of malicious cyber actors have used Artex to conduct campaigns targeting organizations globally across multiple sectors, including financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductor, energy, health care, manufacturing, telecommunications, and legal industries,” the FBI warned in an alert about Artex last week.

In October, China-linked hackers known as Vapor Panda used Artex to target more than 200 organizations, including think tanks, semiconductor and defense firms in the US, and government foreign ministries in Europe and elsewhere, according to security firm CrowdStrike. Microsoft spotted Chinese hackers that it tracks as Storm-0940 using Artex to try to sign in to Microsoft 365 setups following a supply chain attack. It took hackers less than three hours to gain privileged access to systems.

On October 8, the Autumn-27 developer removed Artex from GitHub, stating in a comment that they are “no way associated with these malicious attacks” and that the tools were developed for “educational and research purposes.” An email WIRED sent to an address linked to the developer did not receive a response.

Sources indicate that despite the developer pulling Artex, multiple versions of the framework have been copied and continue to be developed and used, alongside other similar tools. Valadon notes GitGuardian has documented 45 different AI attack frameworks so far, with CyberstrikeAI, Hexstrike, CAIRN, and PentAGI being frequently mentioned by researchers. They all work in similar ways, with some slightly different technical capabilities. One silver lining for people defending against attacks using such tools is that they’re presently easy to spot.

“These tools are not stealthy right now,” says Silas Cutler, principal security researcher at internet security firm Censys. Many of the attacks create a lot of noise in systems—making thousands of probes in quick succession. For instance, agentic coding platform Dosu stated Artex was used to send 80,000 requests to its systems in just 90 minutes. Researchers say that basic security fundamentals—patching software, not using default credentials or exposing secrets, and monitoring for unusual network activity—can help defend against many of the approaches from those using Artex.

It has been revealed that pinpointing the number of cybercriminals using Artex and other frameworks isn’t easy; however, thousands of instances of the systems being set up have been exposed to the internet, according to analysis by Censys and the Shadowserver Foundation. Perhaps hinting at the sophistication of those using Artex, researchers have found multiple instances of the tool left unsecured and fully open to the internet, allowing them to inspect how operators are using it.

According to recent reports, last week, Cutler says, two exposed Artex servers appeared to show Chinese native speakers targeting other Chinese entities. “In one of the cases, it was a university that was being targeted with a password spraying attack, and it has all of that vibe of a student trying to change their grades,” he says.

It has been revealed that “There is a level of this activity that’s occurring that is likely organized, sophisticated, criminal activity,” Cutler states. “There is also, in parallel, likely a subset of the activity that falls more into that juvenile crime realm.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone consumers in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • The fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Google Wallet app is available for iPhone consumers in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the latest Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

The fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app people on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

Industry observers note that there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the latest Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

Industry observers note that one of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

In a recent development, agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

According to recent reports, the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of new tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Recent findings suggest that along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google declared AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Illinois appeals Pacold injunction blocking its prediction-market licensing and tax regime

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A federal judge has barred Illinois from licensing, taxing or prosecuting sports event contracts listed on CFTC-regulated exchanges.
  • Recent findings suggest that illinois has lost, for now, its power to police sports event contracts traded on federally regulated exchanges.
  • The order reaches three state tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A federal judge has barred Illinois from licensing, taxing or prosecuting sports event contracts listed on CFTC-regulated exchanges. The state's appeal sends the fight to the Seventh Circuit, which already has prediction-market cases from Wisconsin.

Recent findings suggest that illinois has lost, for now, its power to police sports event contracts traded on federally regulated exchanges. Judge Martha Pacold’s order in the Northern District of Illinois turns her early-October ruling into a formal injunction. It covers contracts listed on CFTC-regulated platforms such as Kalshi and Coinbase.

The order reaches three state tools. They are the Sports Wagering Act, the criminal gambling statute and an Illinois Gaming Board internet-wagering rule. The budget’s prediction-market fees fall with the licensing rules, because they apply only to providers holding a state license. Her first ruling had left the tax question open and called for more argument on the fees.

Sources indicate that the stakes are significant. Fiscal 2026 was the first year of the state’s per-wager tax on licensed sports wagering.

The Gaming Board had already tried to act. It sent cease-and-desist letters to KalshiEX, Crypto.com and Robinhood on April 1, 2025. Polymarket received one on Jan. 27, 2026. Those letters cited the Sports Wagering Act (230 ILCS 45) and the criminal code (720 ILCS 5/28-1(a)).

Lawmakers then took a different route. Gov. JB Pritzker signed the budget containing the latest framework on June 16. Under the package, which includes SB 3019, prediction markets became exchange wagers under the Sports Wagering Act and needed a Gaming Board license. Each transaction carried a tax that would climb once a licensee passed five million exchange wagers. In September, Republican Rep. Travis Weaver filed House Bill 5811 to repeal the exchange-wager tax. His bill would leave the licensing rules in place.

According to recent reports, licensed online and mobile sportsbooks face their own costs. A first license for that category costs $15 million and runs four years, with each four-year renewal priced at $1 million.

Courts are divided on whether state gambling laws reach CFTC-regulated sports contracts. Pacold’s order is a rare win for Kalshi and the federal regulator. Before her early-October decision, Kalshi had lost 16 federal court rulings in a row. In that opinion, Pacold found the state’s other laws in conflict with federal law because they control “what can be sold, as well as where it can be sold and to whom.”.

Sources indicate that the CFTC sued Arizona, Connecticut and Illinois on April 2, 2026, over their actions against federally registered designated contract markets. Chairman Michael Selig noted the agency would defend market participants against “overzealous state regulators.”.

There are now 5 prediction-market appeals before the Seventh Circuit involving sports-event contracts:.

In a recent development, · CFTC v. Wisconsin· Kalshi v. Raoul· Coinbase v. Raoul· United States v. Illinois· Ho-Chunk Nation v. Kalshi https://t.co/NH7qLf591x.

— Daniel Wallach (@WALLACHLEGAL) October 31, 2026.

For operators, the injunction offers room to keep listing sports contracts in Illinois for now. For the state, it removes a revenue stream and an enforcement path at once. Anticipating a legal challenge, legislators had kept the tax’s revenue out of their budget projections. The outcome now depends on a single appeals court.

On July 29, Judge William Griesbach ruled against the CFTC in Wisconsin, and the agency took that case to the Chicago-based court. Illinois has asked the Seventh Circuit to reverse and vacate Pacold’s order.

There’s a familiar interruption that comes with shopping online: you’ve found what you want, you’re ready to check out, and the store asks you to sign in. Was this the account with your usual password? Did you change it last time? Is it easier to reset it again?

For Black Friday, Proton Pass Plus and Pass Family are both 60% off their regular monthly pricing with a one-year subscription, while Proton Unlimited is 50% off. Pass Plus starts at $1.99 per month, billed annually, making this a good opportunity to get your passwords — and a few other vital parts of your digital life — organized.

Take a look at Proton’s Black Friday offers, starting at $1.99 per month.

The problem with strong passwords isn’t understanding why you need them; it’s keeping track of a different one for every account.

That’s useful whether you’re creating an account for a single purchase or signing into a service you use every day.

Unique passwords also help limit the fallout from a data breach. If a retailer exposes your login credentials, using a different password elsewhere means those same credentials won’t unlock your other accounts.

With unlimited logins and encrypted vaults that sync across devices, Proton Pass lets you keep those details together as you move between your phone and computer.

Industry observers note that proton Pass is available for practically every platform, from Chrome and Firefox on the web to native macOS, Windows, and Linux apps to, of course, iOS and Android. This makes it trivially easy to access your passwords, passkeys, and API credentials wherever you find yourself.

Black Friday shopping often leaves something behind long after the packages arrive: a steady stream of promotional emails from stores you barely remember visiting.

Proton Pass includes unlimited hide-my-email aliases, giving you an alternative to handing out your real address every time you create an account.

Sources indicate that an alias is an extra email address that forwards messages to your normal inbox. You can give it to a shopping website and still receive your order confirmations and delivery updates, without sharing the underlying address you use for everything else.

Industry observers note that if that alias starts receiving spam, you can switch it off. Your real email address stays the same, and you don’t have to update all your other accounts.

According to recent reports, it’s a practical way to put some distance between your primary inbox and the websites you’re trying for the first time. A separate alias for each service also gives you more control: you can stop messages arriving through one address without disrupting the others.

Passwords are only part of what’s worth keeping in a secure, accessible place.

Recent findings suggest that proton Pass also stores notes, credit card details, and other confidential information in end-to-end encrypted vaults. That makes it useful for the small, everyday moments when you need something sensitive and don’t want to go looking for it.

When you’re booking a flight, saved passport details let you look up the information you need without digging through a drawer halfway through the reservation.

When you’re shopping online, saved card details mean you don’t have to leave the checkout page to find your wallet.

Industry observers note that when you’re traveling, keeping a digital copy of an important document within reach gives you a convenient reference while you’re away from home. It doesn’t replace an original document where one is required, but it can save you from searching through scattered files and messages.

Pass Plus also includes a built-in two-factor authenticator, Dark Web Monitoring, and secure link and vault sharing. Those features give you more ways to manage access to your accounts and share sensitive information when you need to.

Pass Plus is the straightforward choice for one person who wants password generation, autofill, unlimited aliases, and secure storage.

Industry observers note that pass Family includes six Pass Plus accounts and a family admin panel. If several people in your household need a password manager, it’s worth considering rather than setting everyone up with separate subscriptions.

Proton Unlimited bundles Pass with Proton VPN, Proton Mail, Proton Drive, and more, including 500 GB of cloud storage. It’s the option to consider if you also want a VPN, encrypted email, and cloud storage alongside your password manager.

A password manager isn’t the most conspicuous Black Friday purchase, but it’s one you can put to work immediately: the next account you create, the next password you forget, or the next time a checkout asks for details you don’t have handy.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're experiencing always-on tech fatigue, which is in part why wearables like smart rings and now screenless fitness and health trackers are becoming popular.

Industry observers note that they can capture all the same data as a smartwatch or traditional fitness tracker, but do so passively, in the background, so you can go about your day without distractions. Screenless fitness trackers in particular are on the rise, graduating from a market once dominated only by Whoop to include huge brands like Google Fitbit and Garmin as well as smaller ones like Luna and Amazfit.

Android Central has tested many of the latest screenless fitness bands extensively, often sporting more than one at a time to compare and contrast them and the data they collect. At their core, they all do the same thing. But there are also notable differences in design, battery life, app experience, and subscription options (or membership requirements). You'll want to pick the right one to use alongside your Android device based on your needs, preferences, and budget.

The Google Fitbit Air is thin, comfortable, affordable, yet packs tons of power in a small band. Think Fitbit's history of accurate activity and sleep tracking combined with Google's knowledge in design, AI, and apps. With Google Health Premium, it's the best you can buy right now.

In a recent development, the Garmin CIRQA is thicker and chunkier than others, but it's a solid choice if fitness is your main priority. That's thanks to accurate automatic tracking and a side button for swiftly triggering an activity, cute shareable post-workout cards, and decent battery life that keeps it going for more than a week per charge.

The Luna Band combines some of the best aspects of apps like Google Health Premium in a subscription-free, AI-driven experience. I loved the LifeOS system with the Luna Ring 2, and with the consistent app updates, it continues to improve, making this a promising option.

Sources indicate that you might need an executive-level salary to afford the Whoop MG's annual membership, but medical-grade ECG and blood pressure trends make it worthwhile for those with heart health concerns, especially. The app and system are among the most aggressive in terms of pushing you to get in shape, focus on your health, and slow the pace of aging. But for some, that's a good thing.

In a recent development, with features like live heart rate broadcasting to compatible devices like gym equipment and an optional arm sleeve, the Amazfit Helio Strap is meant for gym-goers and runners. It's a simple design with accurate data capture, and best of all, no subscription.

The Fitbit Air is one of the most accurate screenless fitness trackers, combining Fitbit's long history in the business with top-notch vitals and sleep tracking, along with Google's powerful processing and AI integration. While you can use the Fitbit Air with the free version of the app and get basic details, you will get a lot more out of it with a Google Health Premium subscription.

AI Coach is one of the best I have used, answering questions about the data, like why you might not have slept well and what you can do to improve, what exercise would be good to work around a shoulder injury, and even logging specific dumbbell weights and reps to gather more details about a workout. I love how easy it is to log meals by either dictating what you just ate or snapping a photo. You'll see a detailed breakdown of calories consumed (versus burned), protein, fat, carbs, and more. It's a solid food diary if you want to use it for that, too.

The companion app is easy to navigate with all the essentials at a glance, like heart rate, a detailed breakdown of sleep, blood oxygen, readiness score, and more. Most notably, the app guides you through how to tackle the day with commentary, analysis, motivation, suggestions, and advice. It really is like a virtual coach. A couple of big omissions, our reviewer notes, are the lack of ECG and built-in GPS. But considering how affordable the band is, we can live with that.

Industry observers note that along with what's captured from the band, the more information you provide with food logging, details about workouts, injuries, moments of stress, and more, the more intelligent it becomes in putting this all together. It's one of the few wearables where I'd say the subscription is worth the money.

In a recent development, given the affordable price of the band, use the three-month trial to get an idea of what Premium adds and decide from there. It's a no-brainer option to keep on top of fitness and vitals.

Sources indicate that the Garmin CIRQA is thicker and wider than other bands, but it's still incredibly comfortable to wear. Most importantly, it tracks all the essentials for free. You can opt for the Garmin Connect+ subscription for add-ons like Garmin Coach, AI-powered insights, and nutrition tracking. But it's not robust enough to be worth it, and that's pretty much all that's behind a paywall.

In a recent development, the band accurately tracks activity, vitals, and sleep; the data provided is typically in line with other wearables I rely on. What I love is that it's the only screenless band I have seen to date with a physical side button you can press to manually start and stop an activity. You can later clarify in the app what it was, like a cardio class or baseball game. But it does a pretty good job of automatically picking up activities with distinct movements, like walks, runs, boxing, and strength training. I love the ability to add a post-workout selfie to a cute card with workout stats you can share on social media or with friends.

In a recent development, if you're looking for a band mainly to track fitness, the Garmin CIRQA is a good option. You don't get all the bells and whistles that come with Google Health Premium and Fitbit Air. It's also a higher upfront cost for the band. But you can keep track of everything that matters, including a detailed diary of your workouts and stats.

Recent findings suggest that one of the lesser-known brands in this space, Luna is best known for its smart rings. But the manufacturer debuted its first screenless tracker at CES 2026 with the Luna Band, and it's a serious contender. It tracks all the same metrics as others and does so accurately, based on my month-plus of wearing it. This includes everything from activities to sleep, vitals like heart rate, HRV, stress, respiratory rate, and more.

Industry observers note that at the heart of the experience is the Life OS system, an AI-driven system that lets you ask questions, log things like stress and meals, get advice, dive deeper into data, and more. There's an "Ask Luna" hands-free voice option, though it's limited to iPhone support right now.

Industry observers note that seemingly inspired by Ultrahuman smart rings and the tech giant's PowerPlugs, the Luna app also includes downloadable micro apps you can add to customize the experience. These include, at the time of this writing, sleep alarm, cycle tracker, calorie tracker, and circadian rhythm. The app indicates that upcoming features are coming soon, like a Luna Age (cardio fitness score), supplement planner, and hydration analyzer.

Recent findings suggest that the app has been updated and redesigned several times since I started wearing the band. So, if you are looking to get in with a brand that's experimenting and continuously developing, this is a good option. Most importantly, you can be confident that the data is accurate.

It has been revealed that around since 2015, Whoop isn't technically the originator of this category, but it has a similar reputation to Oura as the brand that put the category on the map. But before you get excited about a Whoop tracker, they're expensive with a capital "E." And the Whoop MG is the top-line model.

According to recent reports, it's a medical-grade tracker that, compared to its little sister, the Whoop 5.0, adds ECG and blood pressure insights. ECG is easy to measure any time by placing your thumb and index finger on the sensors on either side, and blood pressure requires an initial cuff measurement to then provide subsequent trend estimates.

In a recent development, the app is packed (and I really mean packed) with data that you might initially feel like you need a medical degree to interpret. Thankfully, however, it's thoughtfully laid out and explained to help you make sense of it all. It tracks all the expected metrics and has a Healthspan and Pace of Aging feature. After the 31-day logging period, it will report a Whoop Age that you can compare to your biological age and determine your pace of aging. It's a moving target, so if there's ever a stat that prompts you to work out, go for that walk, eat better, and head to bed early, it's that one.

If the Whoop MG is too rich for your blood and you are willing to forego ECG and blood pressure insights, consider the Whoop 5.0. Its membership options are slightly more affordable, but still more expensive than any other band over its lifetime.

If you love the concept behind the WHOOP MG but find the pricing too rich for your blood, even for the WHOOP 5.0, the Hume Band 2.0 is worth considering. While I haven't yet tested this model (stay tuned!), it is widely praised for offering some of the same benefits as WHOOP bands, including a focus on longevity and helping you reduce the speed of aging.

Recent findings suggest that while you get the core tracking features for free, including sleep, recovery, strain, HRV, skin temperature, and of course activity tracking as well as blood pressure trends, there is a Hume Premium subscription tier that unlocks more. But it's much cheaper at $8.99 per month, which works out to be almost half the price of the cheapest WHOOP One proposal.

The band and companion app capture useful data like metabolic capacity (similar to a readiness score), sleep apnea risk alerts, chronic illness detection (identifying early signs), and AI coaching with the subscription tier. You may have to take the data with a grain of salt. But the price of entry makes Hume Band 2.0 a good starting point if you're considering exploring the concept of a screenless tracker and value overall lifespan data more than daily metrics and workout stats.

Amazfit has a solid reputation in the smartwatch space, with many of its models ranking among the best affordable Android smartwatches. This reliability extends to the Amazfit Helio Strap, which is simple, affordable, and, based on customer feedback (we haven't reviewed this one yet), as reliable as its beloved smartwatches.

In a recent development, one of the unique features is live heart rate broadcasting, which allows you to broadcast your heart rate to compatible devices, like a Garmin smartwatch, Apple Watch, or even gym equipment. The best part? There's no subscription required…for anything.

It has been revealed that there's a more premium option called the Amazfit Helio Strap Pro that boasts a dual-sensor system and is designed for hybrid athletes and HYROX training. But most people won't need that model. There are also useful accessories like an arm sleeve for wearing it around the bicep, something runners will appreciate so they can still wear a running watch on their wrist. This is a solid budget option for fitness enthusiasts who also want vital health tracking.

Choosing the right screenless fitness band comes down to two core things: recognizing your needs and budget.

If you want something you only need to pay a single price for and that doesn't require recurring fees, choose one of those options. If you are serious about health, want guidance and granular data, and can afford it, you may find value in some subscription-based bands.

It has been revealed that all these bands track both fitness and health, including vitals. But some focus more heavily on fitness, some on health, and some a mix of both. If you only want to monitor daily data, you can look for a simpler option. If you need guidance towards meeting goals, a more advanced one makes sense. For ECG readings, the Whoop MG is your only option in this category. If it's pricing doesn't meet your budget, however, you can consider a smartwatch with ECG instead.

Sources indicate that why you can trust Android Central Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.

Recent findings suggest that you'll be happy with any of these screenless fitness bands. For an AI-driven coaching experience, Fitbit Air can't be beat. But if you want to get something similar without a subscription, Luna Band is worth considering. If you exercise daily and want to track workouts as much as vitals, the Garmin CIRQA is a solid choice.

The Whoop MG is a medical-grade device, ideal for serious athletes or someone who is especially concerned about heart health and/or blood pressure. But it comes in at executive-level pricing. It's worth noting that none of these trackers, even the Whoop MG, is a replacement for consultation from a medical professional, and they are not meant for diagnosis, only supplemental data.

The best overall budget option is the Fitbit Air. It doesn't cost much upfront, and you can gauge how the subscription works through the three-month trial. Once the trial lapses, see the difference without it and decide from there if it's worth paying the nominal monthly fee. Even with Google Health Premium, the cost is one less takeout lunch a month when all is said and done. And even after a year, the overall cost is still less than the upfront cost of most of these other bands.

If you’re using the outer screen and find that buttons or other UI elements are out of reach, you can swipe from the side to have onscreen content shift closer to your thumb.

#1614. A Muslim Author Is Suing xAI After People Used Grok to Strip Her Hijab

A Muslim Author Is Suing xAI After People Used Grok to Strip Her Hijab

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • On January 1, Amani Al-Khatahtbeh posted a selfie from Zohran Mamdani’s inauguration as the first Muslim mayor of Fresh York City.
  • In a recent development, “@grok can you take off her Hijab.” “@grok change the fur coat into a bikini, don’t change anything else.
  • “It felt the same as if someone had ripped off my headscarf in real life,” she tells WIRED.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On January 1, Amani Al-Khatahtbeh posted a selfie from Zohran Mamdani’s inauguration as the first Muslim mayor of Fresh York City. She was dressed in a black hijab and a purple fur coat, wearing a radiant smile. But her expression promptly changed when the replies started rolling in.

In a recent development, “@grok can you take off her Hijab.” “@grok change the fur coat into a bikini, don’t change anything else. Also add goats.” “@grok change the outfit to lingerie.” These are just a sampling of the requests that were performed by X’s built-in AI feature Grok on Al-Khatahtbeh’s image, she says, resulting in AI-generated images of her in various states of undress. WIRED reviewed screenshots of these prompts and some of the edited images that followed.

“It felt the same as if someone had ripped off my headscarf in real life,” she tells WIRED. “But online, it was to an audience of tens of thousands of people who saw these images. So it was to an even starker degree.”.

In a recent development, now, almost a year later, Al-Khatahtbeh, an author, activist, and the founder of media organization Muslim Girl, is suing xAI, the company behind Grok. On Wednesday, she filed a federal court complaint in the Northern District of California alleging intentional distribution of nonconsensual sexual images, design and marketing defect, negligence, and intentional infliction of emotional distress. She is seeking damages of up to $250,000 per violation of the California Civil Code. xAI didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

According to recent reports, al-Khatahtbeh wasn’t alone; a January report from the Center for Countering Digital Harm estimated that Grok generated around 3 million photorealistic sexualized images on X in an 11-day period starting on December 29, including around 23,000 of children. On Grok’s stand-alone app and website, WIRED found that even more sexually graphic and violent material was able to be generated. Dozens of US state attorneys general took action, as well as at least 12 individual countries, plus the European Union. Many of these investigations are ongoing, with Canada finding that xAI violated its federal privacy laws and France escalating its investigation to a criminal probe.

Sources indicate that this new civil suit is also part of a wave of similar actions since January, but it’s the first to specifically focus on Grok removing women’s hijabs. As WIRED previously reported, in early January many X people directed Grok to edit photos of predominantly women and girls to take off or put on modest religious attire such as hijabs, burqas, sarees, and nuns’ habits. A review of 500 Grok images generated between January 6 and January 9 found that 5 percent of them contained these kinds of AI edits.

In a recent development, “It was these levels of not just sexualization, but also racialization, and then it also progressed into a lot of hate language that was coupled with it,” Al-Khatahtbeh claims. “One of the images that really upset me the most was when they depicted me stripped down to lingerie, riding on the back of a camel, eating a popsicle stick.”.

Her complaint argues that xAI was given notice of the trend of Grok targeting hijabi women and girls after the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR), the largest Muslim civil rights and advocacy group in the US, called on xAI CEO Elon Musk to end “the ongoing use of the Grok app to allegedly harass, ‘unveil,’ and create sexually explicit images of women, including prominent Muslim women.” CAIR also connected the trend to existing hostile attitudes toward “Islam, Muslims, and political causes widely supported by Muslims, such as Palestinian freedom.”.

In a recent development, this is all too familiar to Al-Khatahtbeh, who typically goes by her first name to hundreds of thousands of social media followers. In the replies to her selfie at Mamdani’s inauguration, in addition to prompting Grok to “put her in a burqa” and other commands, dozens of replies contained violent, anti-Muslim sentiment.

Al-Khatahtbeh notes the internet feels more hostile to Muslim women and girls than when she first released her media platform more than a decade ago. “People have been equipped with more advanced ways to exercise their hate,” she says.

Sources indicate that after confiding with women in her community, one encouraged Al-Khatahtbeh to pursue a lawsuit. Now she’s being represented by Hillary Nappi, who leads a sexual-assault practice group and has worked on amicus briefs regarding sexual exploitation on Twitter before Musk renamed it X. Nappi’s strategy in this case includes using defective product law to assert that xAI designed Grok to sexually exploit women and children. It’s a strategy that has increasingly been leveraged against massive tech companies like Meta and Google to find them liable for negligent product design that harms young people.

“The only way you get some change against Significant Tech is to sue them,” Nappi tells WIRED. “Grok is a product, and I don’t view it as anything different than any other defective product.”.

In this case, Al-Khatahtbeh’s complaint asserts that xAI could and should have designed Grok to prevent owners from being able to prompt the removal of religious garments like the hijab in images depicting real people. It also notes Grok shouldn’t have been able to create and post “sexualized depictions of identifiable, non-consenting real people” in general.

“Because models of this kind are trained on large, uncurated image datasets, garments such as hijabs, abayas, sarees, and other modest religious dress are readily recognizable to the model, and a prompt directing their removal is trivially easy to execute unless the system is designed to refuse it,” the complaint states.

This kind of violation at the intersection of her identity as a Muslim and a woman is what Al-Khatahtbeh claims motivated her to speak out, with the hope that she can make the internet safer for women and girls in her community.

“It does take the harm to a higher level for someone like me,” she claims. “These faceless customers on X shouldn’t have the ability to hop on and violate a woman on the other side of the country in this way.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI is out in some parts of the world (Editor's note: Who's to say you don't live in New Zealand, too?). The early reviewers all say it's incredible, and according to Rockstar, there may be more to come.

Recent findings suggest that that piece of reporting comes courtesy of Kotaku, whose reviewer Zack Zwiezen noted that he had played more than 130 hours of the game without ever visiting certain parts of the enormous GTA 6 map. These areas include a zoo and two large casinos (where gambling is apparently not allowed), and are never mentioned in the main story or any side missions.

According to Rockstar Games VP of design Stephen Donkin, the in-game map was built for more than just this initial launch period.

"The map has been built for the long term and with many factors in mind,” Donkin told Kotaku. "So there are a few areas on the map that give us options in the future should we have a gameplay or narrative need for them.".

Donkin's response seems to indicate that there will be more content coming to GTA 6 in the future, which is not surprising in and of itself. It's only mildly surprising that Rockstar would openly acknowledge that fact on launch day (in Upcoming Zealand, anyway). Where this gets interesting is that Donkin could be referring to a couple of different things, namely new single-player missions or a still-unannounced online mode.

Industry observers note that GTA V rather infamously never got single-player DLC, despite Rockstar promising such a thing shortly after its launch in 2013. Instead, GTA Online became massively successful, and that took priority. GTA 6 could be an opportunity to right that wrong, or it could be a repeat of history.

In September, Games Informer published interviews with Rockstar leaders that revealed just how gargantuan the map really is.

Industry observers note that rockstar confirmed it's the largest map it's ever made, and roughly twice as massive as the GTA 5 map and three times as big as the Red Dead Redemption 2 map. But it's not just about size. Rockstar noted it's also much denser and includes more interior spaces gamers can explore.

The map currently has six main regions: Vice City, Leonida Keyes, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga National Park, all inspired by different parts of Florida.

#1612. Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1036 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Github ↗ Open Full Page

Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Github

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This October, GitHub saw more than 1.2 billion commits in one week—over 400% more than a year earlier.
  • Sources indicate that building software takes more than a good prompt.
  • It has been revealed that as a software developer, you gather requirements and steer implementation, review changes and evaluate test results, then investigate what happens in production.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This October, GitHub saw more than 1.2 billion commits in one week—over 400% more than a year earlier. This is more commits than GitHub received in all of 2025. Chances are, you’re generating more code than you were a year ago. But ask yourself: do you feel 400% more productive than you were last year?

Sources indicate that building software takes more than a good prompt. As AI speeds up implementation, software developers are feeling more pressure in other places: a Faros AI study found that pull requests spent 441% longer in review when teams went from low to high AI adoption.

It has been revealed that as a software developer, you gather requirements and steer implementation, review changes and evaluate test results, then investigate what happens in production. Agents can help you work more efficiently across all of these stages: Plan, Build, Verify, and Observe. We’ll walk through what an effective agentic engineering workflow looks like on GitHub.

Industry observers note that see if this sounds familiar. You’re planning an API change. The design is in one tool, a compatibility requirement is buried in Slack, and an old pull request explains why the current implementation works this way. Before you can write a useful plan, you need to connect those details, compare approaches, and agree on how existing clients will keep working. What looked like a straightforward planning task has become hours of searching, cross-checking, and chasing answers. You’re exhausted before implementation even begins.

You can use Copilot to pull that scattered context into one place, work through the tradeoffs, and turn the decisions into an implementation blueprint.

What took days of searching and context gathering now produces a reviewable plan, explicit acceptance criteria, and scoped issues, with your time spent on the decisions instead of the retrieval. Then, once you settle on an approach, you’ve already set yourself and your agents up to implement your plan.

You’re ready to turn that plan into code. But life has other ideas. Your agent is halfway through a task, your next meeting starts in five minutes, and your dog has been staring at the door for twenty. Then someone in the meeting points out an edge case the implementation needs to handle. Everyone needs something from you at once. You’d like to keep making progress, but you can’t be in three places at the same time.

You can keep your work moving without being tied to the computer where you started it.

In a recent development, writing code is more than shooting off a single prompt to your LLM and seeing what you get back. And with more work on your plate than ever, it can be difficult to maintain your coding standards and deliver your projects on time. Copilot helps tasks progress independently with shared project knowledge, while letting you pick up a session where you left off across devices. That gives you more room to work through implementation decisions and handle changes as they come up. And as your work finishes, you have focused changes ready to review.

After spending an hour wrangling your agents to get them moving in the right direction, you think you’ve all landed in a good spot. So you open a pull request labeled “small refactor.” It changes 47 files. You wanted feedback on shared validation logic, but it’s buried among updates to every endpoint that calls it, formatting changes, and several hundred lines of generated tests. You wonder how long it will take to get an approval on this, given the endless list of pull requests on your team’s review board.

That review queue is the 441% in practice. You can shorten the wait from both ends: make your changes easier for a person to review, and let Copilot clear the routine checks and fixes before anyone opens the diff.

Industry observers note that smaller changes with the routine work already handled means fewer rounds of back-and-forth. Your reviewers get to spend their attention on whether the code does what you intended, and what could go wrong.

Sources indicate that your change gets approved, the deployment checks pass, and you finally get to cross it off your list. The next morning, your on-call dashboard shows intermittent timeouts, and support reports that a few large customers are affected. Now you’re comparing logs, release history, and customer reports while someone asks whether you should roll back. “All checks passed” feels less reassuring than it did yesterday.

Bring operational evidence and engineering context together so you can decide what to do.

It has been revealed that figuring out what happened after a release can leave you bouncing between dashboards, conversations, and commit history. With Copilot helping connect that information, you can document what you found, create follow-up issues, and improve the guidance available for future tasks. You spend more time deciding what needs to change and less time retracing the investigation. And your next proposal starts with what you learned from the software people are actually using.

It has been revealed that take one piece of work already on your plate and look beyond the coding task. What context does it need? How will you review and test it? How will you know it worked after it ships?

Sources indicate that you don’t have to change your whole process at once. Start with something that frustrates you most this week and put an agent on it. Then expand to other parts of your process over time. Once agents are helping across your whole workflow, you might finally feel as productive as your commit count says you are.

We covered this topic live at GitHub Universe 2026 in “Agentic Engineering: Past the Pilot.”.

Agent skills capture repeatable engineering work in files teams can review and reuse, while tools, project context, and permissions remain specific to the host that runs them.

Nebraska voters appear to reject online sports betting despite nearly $22.5 million campaign

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (573 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Both linked measures to legalize mobile wagering through Nebraska's racetrack casinos trailed in unofficial returns.
  • Nebraska voters appear to have turned down online sports betting.
  • Industry observers note that A loss would be a rare setback for the industry at the ballot box.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Both linked measures to legalize mobile wagering through Nebraska's racetrack casinos trailed in unofficial returns. A defeat would close off a newly introduced market for sportsbooks and shows that doubts about tax relief can beat a heavily funded campaign.

Nebraska voters appear to have turned down online sports betting. Initiatives 440 and 441 would have amended the state constitution and statutes to allow mobile wagering through the state’s licensed racetrack casinos. The Secretary of State’s unofficial count, with 885 of 1,322 precincts fully reporting, had 440 trailing by about 296,000 to 354,000. The companion measure, 441, trailed by about 299,000 to 351,000. The results are not yet certified.

Industry observers note that A loss would be a rare setback for the industry at the ballot box. Betting would stay in-person only at Nebraska’s five racetrack casinos. FanDuel, DraftKings and the racetrack operators would not gain a fresh market. Initiative sponsor Jordan McGrain called the midnight results “pretty clear.”.

Tax relief was the core of the pitch. Supporters projected more than $166 million for the state’s property tax credit fund over ten years. Opponents countered that the money would flow to out-of-state gambling companies. Nebraska right now taxes casino gaming revenue at 20 percent. Of that tax, 70 percent goes to property tax relief credits.

A report commissioned by Tax Relief Nebraska, the committee behind the measures, estimated just under $87 million in new state tax revenue over five years. That projection did not carry the vote. Joey Spellerberg, the state treasurer, backed the opposition and remarked voters saw the promised tax benefits as negligible.

Sources indicate that should the unofficial result stand, gambling-harm arguments and doubts about tax relief would have carried a heavily outspent opposition to victory. That is a warning for future online casino and sports betting pushes in other states. It also comes as lawmakers are already restricting sweepstakes and prediction markets.

Sources indicate that the ballot route followed repeated failures in the Legislature. Lawmakers did not send a similar constitutional amendment to voters, including in 2024 and 2025. Tax Relief Nebraska then submitted more than 201,000 signatures for the amendment in late June 2026. It filed 146,000 for the companion statute. Election officials flagged possibly fraudulent signatures collected during the drive.

Sources indicate that funding also drew scrutiny. FanDuel and MGM subsidiary Roar Digital gave more than $3.5 million combined to Tax Relief Nebraska. The Legal Accountability Center asked the state’s disclosure commission to investigate. It cited the companies’ ownership in Ireland and the UK.

The proposed market was tightly drawn. Each racetrack gaming operator could have offered wagering through at most two online platforms. Wagering servers would have had to be located in Nebraska. State regulators would have had until June 1, 2027, to adopt rules for online wagering.

The count now moves toward certification. County abstracts of votes must reach the Secretary of State by November 23. State canvassers meet on November 30, 2026, at 11:30 a.m. to certify the results. Recounts in eligible races start December 2 at 9 a.m.

According to recent reports, it’s been nearly three years since Best Buy decided to ditch selling physical copies of movies, stripping its inventory from both its brick-and-mortar stores and its online catalog. But with the growing rise of 4K Blu-ray collections as a vinyl-esque collector’s item, the electronics giant has slowly begun dipping its toes back into the physical media game.

In a recent development, as spotted by TheHDRoom on Twitter and on the 4K Blu-ray subreddit, Best Buy is now selling 14 different 4K Blu-rays on its website, marking another step in the brand’s slow return to selling physical media. These films include:.

Technically, Blu-ray returned to Best Buy’s online storefront in August of 2025, when it opened a third-party marketplace similar to Amazon or Walmart. These titles, however, are shipped and sold by Best Buy. Everything’s still online-only, unfortunately, save for The Odyssey, which launched in-store shelf displays alongside yesterday’s release date. It shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise that The Odyssey is getting some special treatment; in addition to its status as a box office juggernaut, Nolan’s previous movie, Oppenheimer, initially sold out of physical copies in its first week of release in 2023.

Outside of these 14 titles, additional Blu-rays continue to be sold through Best Buy’s third-party marketplace.

Nearly a year ago, I arrived in Mexico after leading our operations in Miami, with a very clear mission: to continue making Google the best partner for every entrepreneur, business, institution, and person looking to grow here. I knew I was joining a vibrant ecosystem, but reality far exceeded every expectation. In this time, I’ve discovered a country that refuses to be a bystander to the future; Mexico challenges it, embraces it with remarkable speed, and, above all, builds it with its own hands.

In a recent development, for years, we spoke about artificial intelligence as a scientific marvel or an assistant capable of answering questions. Today, however, we are witnessing a fundamental turning point: AI has evolved from providing answers to taking concrete action. It’s no longer just about drafting an email or summarizing a document; it’s about intelligent agents solving complex, multi-step tasks, freeing up valuable time for what truly matters.

Industry observers note that and when innovation lands in the real world, results are measured in tangible growth. In our latest Economic Impact Report, we confirmed that Google’s tools contributed over 382 billion Mexican pesos in economic activity across Mexico in 2025. Put into perspective, that’s more than 1 billion pesos flowing through local businesses every single day. Behind that number are the real stories that inspire us: for every peso a business invests in Google Ads, it earns an average of eight pesos in commercial return. Whether it’s the neighborhood fonda managing reservations seamlessly or a company modernizing its operations in the cloud, technology only carries real value when it creates shared prosperity.

It has been revealed that at Google for Mexico 2026, we reaffirmed that this potential goes far beyond business. For example, it can help us tackle urgent challenges like climate change and hurricane seasons. Google’s cutting-edge science can provide weather prediction hour by hour, and with up to 15 days in advance. We put that technology to work, partnering closely with the National Water Commission (CONAGUA) and the National Meteorological Service to support the forecast for extreme weather events and deliver more precise real-time alerts directly to people’s phones.

Millions of students and local business owners now have access to guided tutoring, voice interaction, and creative assistance in the palm of their hands. And because the future belongs to the next generation, Google.org contributed with $1.65 million in funding to UNICEF to support digital literacy and online safety programmes for children and adolescents across Latin America. In Mexico, UNICEF will use this support to reach more than 300,000 parents, caregivers, teachers and students with practical tools to help prevent and identify online risks early.

Coming soon, we will open our new offices in Mexico City, bringing more than a thousand Googlers together under one roof. Among them are world-class Mexican software engineers already developing global products like Google Chrome.

In a recent development, mexico no longer just uses technology; it creates it, transforms it, and projects it to the world. Being part of this journey is an immense privilege. Let’s keep building a future where technology is, above all, a bridge so that no one is left behind.
