Review: Amazon’s Alexa Tablet 8 is a Fire Tablet with Google Play for $150 – what’s not to love?

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amazon shocked everyone in October when it released its newly introduced Alexa Tablet series with Google Play support built-in, addressing the biggest shortcoming of its older Fire Tablets.
  • According to recent reports, the Alexa Tablet 8 is one of three latest Amazon tablets that introduced in October with Google Play on board, and it’s also the one I was personally the most excited about.
  • Right up there with Amazon’s long-running reputation in the tablet space, Alexa Tablet 8 is very much an affordable device, and that’s reflected in its fairly meager specs:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon shocked everyone in October when it released its newly introduced Alexa Tablet series with Google Play support built-in, addressing the biggest shortcoming of its older Fire Tablets. For Black Friday 2026, the Alexa Tablet 8 is a mere $150 and, with Google Play on board, this feels like a Fire Tablet that’s all grown up.

According to recent reports, the Alexa Tablet 8 is one of three latest Amazon tablets that introduced in October with Google Play on board, and it’s also the one I was personally the most excited about. I love a good tiny Android tablet, but there just aren’t that many out there – and some of the ones we do have are exorbitantly expensive.

Right up there with Amazon’s long-running reputation in the tablet space, Alexa Tablet 8 is very much an affordable device, and that’s reflected in its fairly meager specs:.

Yet, I didn’t find myself put off by the device.

I specifically asked Amazon for a review unit of the absolute base model – 4GB of RAM and lockscreen ads – and I can say with confidence it’s Not Bad at the end of the day.

The display is objectively not good, but it’s not really trying to be flashy either. The panel gets bright enough for most indoor use and, for general browsing or watching videos around the house or even on a flight, it gets the job done. If anything, my biggest complaint on the display was just how smudgey it gets with fingerprints.

Sources indicate that hardware is a strong suit. The Alexa Tablet 8 has an aluminum build that comes in this gorgeous teal color as well as a softer “Rosette” pink (or “Graphite,” if you want to keep it boring). It’s thin and light and slips into a bag easily, and even fit into the back pocket of my jeans. Buttons are clicky and aspects such as the speakers actually do well enough – like the display, the speakers aren’t good, but they’re not bad by any stretch either.

Amazon has a folio cover available that’s simple but nice, with a fabric finish that’s grippy. It’s an extra $40, though, which feels like a bit much for a super-affordable Android slate.

The biggest question was around the software experience, and this is where this fresh effort really shines.

In a recent development, alexa Tablet 8 ships with Android 16 out of the box, not FireOS or whatever Amazon was calling its forked experience on Fire Tablets (I genuinely refuse to go double-check because it’s a memory I’m thrilled to never have to revisit). It’s a pretty “stock” experience, with Amazon leaving aspects such as the notification shade/quick settings alone, and even the Settings menu feels pretty clean.

That’s not to say nothing has changed. The homescreen has a fairly standard layout , but with these neat little corner widgets – one a “dynamic” widget with scrolling content (mostly ads) and the other a shortcut for Alexa search. Amazon is pushing Alexa as a voice assistant pretty heavily on these tablets, but I’m happy to report it’s pretty easy to ignore if you choose. These tablets will be great additions to your Alexa ecosystem if you’re invested, but I’m simply not.

The biggest change you’ll find is the lockscreen, where Amazon’s base models all come with lockscreen ads. This saves you about $20 on the hardware, and it’s not that bad of an experience. That stated, I’d absolutely spend the extra $20 at purchase to go without them, especially seeing as this blocks the ability to set a lockscreen wallpaper at all. It doesn’t cost anything more to remove them later, though, with a $20 charge through your Amazon account removing ads.

But what’s vital here is that, for the fire time, Amazon is admitting defeat and installing the Google Play Store.

According to recent reports, alexa Tablet 8, and the rest of the lineup, has Google Play out of the box and access to any app you want. This means that you can, if you choose, fully ignore Amazon’s own services and do whatever you want. The smallest of examples: While Amazon’s built-in keyboard is fine, it’s wonderful that I don’t have to jump through hoops to switch over to Gboard. Fire Tablets were always an enticing value with a big catch, but Amazon’s change in this regard truly makes Alexa Tablets an attractive option for everyone – not just those willing to put up with the restriction or put in the work to hack Google apps on board.

Industry observers note that performance, despite the meager specs, is not awful. MediaTek’s low-end chip has just enough horsepower for general use, and 4GB of RAM isn’t as detrimental as I would have expected. It’s not fast by any means, but you could do a lot worse. There are 4GB Android tablets I’ve literally decided not to review because I couldn’t use them past the setup process, so the fact that Amazon is delivering a completely usable experience is a win in my book, even more so that I don’t actually mind using it. There’s a caveat to that, of course, and it’s that you shouldn’t expect to do a ton on this base model. For light browsing, reading Kindle books (or whatever other reading app since, you know, Google Play), or watching videos, this is great. For games, you’ll want to look elsewhere (and expect to spend more).

“Not awful” is kind of the pattern here.

In a recent development, alexa Tablet 8 isn’t some shining example of a perfect budget tablet, but I think it really nails the fundamentals. At its usual $230~ starting price, it’s a plenty-good deal for those in the market for an affordable Android slate, but the Black Friday pricing of just $150 is all the better – I just wish the model with 8GB of RAM was also on sale.

Amazon’s pivot to Alexa Tablets is great – though I hope the company knows full well that everyone is still going to call these Fire Tablets or Kindles or whatever combination of brands that spring to mind. But that reputation might work in Amazon’s favor at the end of the day. While there’s a huge portion of the audience that’s been left frustrated for years at the lack of Play Store support on Fire Tablets, they’ve still been a market success for the most part, so this shift is just a win for everyone. Owners get a better experience, Amazon gets to shuffle its priorities away from a dead app store, and the market as a whole gets an affordable piece of hardware that doesn’t suck.

The ‘GTA 6’ Work Blackout Is Here

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Somewhere out there, right at this moment, a couple is probably still negotiating the final terms of a contract that permits one partner to play Grand Theft Auto VI around the clock for an entire week following its Thursday release.
  • So don’t be surprised if a console owner in your life is curiously unavailable between now and Thanksgiving.
  • Recent findings suggest that especially within the tech and gaming industries, the expectation is that many developers won’t be clocking in on Thursday or Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somewhere out there, right at this moment, a couple is probably still negotiating the final terms of a contract that permits one partner to play Grand Theft Auto VI around the clock for an entire week following its Thursday release. Adults who grew up on the felony-based video game franchise are taking steps to secure sick days—and some, no doubt, are granting their own kids permission to stay home from school (despite warnings from their teachers). Streamers on Twitch and YouTube stand ready to conquer the enhanced and expanded virtual domain of Vice City, seeking out every last Easter egg.

So don’t be surprised if a console owner in your life is curiously unavailable between now and Thanksgiving. The 13-year-wait for this latest installment of the series has felt interminable enough to inspire a meme used in reaction to any surprising or unprecedented news: “We got [fill in the blank] before GTA VI.”.

Recent findings suggest that especially within the tech and gaming industries, the expectation is that many developers won’t be clocking in on Thursday or Friday. (GTA VI officially releases for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S at midnight local time on Thursday, November 19, according to publisher Rockstar Games.).

“I’m not going to question whether folks are really sick on their sick days or how they spend a vacation day,” notes Mike, an executive of a gaming studio with more than a thousand employees, who requested a pseudonym to avoid damaging professional relationships within the industry. “I want them to spend time engaging with the medium we love, and there’s no question that playing lots of video games helps you make video games.”.

In October, the HR software firm BambooHR concluded through data analysis and a survey of salaried workers that the PTO request rate for November 19 is nearly 13 percent higher than equivalent days in past years, while Xbox is running a promotional campaign in which gamers can generate notes from a Dr. Xbox (DJ Khaled in glasses and a lab coat) claiming that they have a “Vitamin G” deficiency and are unable to work.

A few companies are getting ahead of the productivity slump; the hardware and software manufacturer Logitech, for example, declared earlier this month that all 7,000 employees would be granted a paid day off for gaming, to be scheduled any time within a year or so. In announcing the policy, the organization cited internal studies on the ways that gaming may potentially improve job performance and mental health.

Riot Games, the publisher behind League of Legends and Valorant, has likewise made arrangements for the blockbuster event. “We have an open PTO policy, and we’ve seen leaders encourage their teams to enjoy the first day of release,” Joe Hixson, Riot Games vice president of communications, tells WIRED. “On our main campus, we'll be celebrating with a special-themed lunch menu and snacks that pay homage to the game. We also expect to see people firing it up in our console rooms during breaks and after hours.”.

Sources indicate that riot additionally offers the Play Fund, a stipend of $25 a month for employees to spend on gaming titles across platforms and genres. “It makes us better developers by deepening our understanding of what makes a great player experience,” Hixson states.

Mike tells WIRED that on in-office workdays, the firm has a typical absentee rate of 5 to 7 percent due to vacations, illness, travel, and the like. He estimates that on Thursday, it will be more like 10 or 12 percent. “Now, on the Friday, will there be some number of employees who are ‘working’ when they’re at home but also suspiciously slow to answer messages while they have substantial chunks of their calendar blocked out for ‘deep individual work?’” says the studio leader. “Yeah, probably.”.

According to recent reports, but it’s hardly unusual in the business for people to select their days off to accommodate a major game release, Mike says. In 2023, he was out for three days to play The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, which he recalls as “paradise.”.

That mentioned, he notes that the next leap forward for GTA is no ordinary affair. The hype for this franchise, he explains, “breaks containment,” reaching people who have not bought a latest title in years.

Recent findings suggest that that’s why even companies without ties to gaming culture have been making allowances for so-called Grand Theft Auto Flu. On Monday, the social team for the luxury real estate firm Serhant posted a video of CEO Ryan Serhant (also the host of the Netflix reality show Owning Manhattan) agreeing with an employee that if the clip garnered 400,000 likes, the office would close for GTA day. “You’ll never get that,” Serhant predicted.

The post picked up 1.4 million likes within 24 hours, prompting an update on Tuesday: The firm would honor Serhant’s promise. “We are massive supporters of our team, their passions both in and out of real estate, and all things culture and tech,” Serhant said in a statement to WIRED, noting that “13 years of anticipation deserves a day off.” The organization announced a floating holiday to staff on Wednesday, to be used any time before the end of 2026.

Also on Wednesday, Arizona Beverages revealed a sweepstakes for social media followers who may have felt they couldn’t afford to miss a work shift. Dropping a PTO request for GTA day in the comment section, the company stated, would enter that person for a chance to win $500 to cover their lost hours.

Recent findings suggest that with this level of fanfare, nearly 16 million preorders bringing in revenue of $1.5 billion, and expectations of 45 million sales in its launch quarter, GTA VI is poised to be the most significant entertainment event of the year and the biggest video game of all time. It’s little wonder, then, that some have warned about the global economy slowing down this week as fans ignore their email inboxes and Slack messages to indulge in some extended role-play as streetwise criminals. One economist has estimated that the GTA release could cost the US economy $1 billion in lost productivity.

Mike isn’t buying this, however, arguing that the hype about “how GTA will impact the GDP or cause a failure of the power grid or whatever are just silly.” He points out that “PC is the biggest individual platform, and the PC launch timing is still unclear.” Neither have Rockstar and Take-Two announced a launch date for the game’s online multiplayer mode; only the single-player experience will be available on Thursday.

Andy Garin, an associate professor of economics at Carnegie Mellon University, also finds the concerns about sluggish market activity to be overblown.

“Speculation about a hit to productivity around these kinds of events pops up a lot, particularly during the Olympics or World Cup, when time zone differences mean major events are during the workday,” Garin says. “I don't think the release date of GTA VI will be that different than these sort of events that happen all the time, particularly if workers are using their allotted PTO or scheduling flexibility baked into their jobs.”.

Malcolm Robinson, who has a YouTube channel dedicated to gaming and works at a veterans hospital, tells WIRED that the GTA release just happens to fall on his day off. “I blueprint on playing it for about eight to 12 hours straight on the first night,” he says.

Industry observers note that others have had no difficulty setting that time aside. One redditor who works as the distribution coordinator for a chain of auto shops in Colorado and requested anonymity out of concern for professional consequences notes that he would have called in sick on Thursday but had the option to use PTO. His supervisor asked if it was to play GTA, which he confirmed. “He was like, ‘I get it, enjoy,’” this gamer reports. He plans to play along with his girlfriend, who is also taking the day off, and is excited to “sink my teeth into it before the entire thing gets spoiled.”.

In a recent development, james Lord, a data entry coordinator in Edmonton, Alberta, tells WIRED that he initially offered to let his team take Thursday off for GTA purposes. When none of them expressed interest in the game, he states, he “jumped at the opportunity” to claim the day for himself. He’s been playing Grand Theft Auto since the original top-down POV game for the PC came out in the late 1990s.

According to recent reports, lord, too, is wary of spoilers—he locked down his social media on Tuesday night to avoid any—but nostalgia and lifelong relationships are even better reasons to jump into GTA VI as soon as he can. He’s going to boot up the game while on a call with his brother, who lives across the country, and they’ll be joined by friends living in Pennsylvania and Texas. It’s a reunion experience that wouldn’t be possible without a break from the 9-to-5 job.

“We lead busy lives now,” Lord reflects, “so having to set time aside for the game of the decade is important to us.”.

Snapchat now lets developers build AR Lenses with AI assistants like Claude Code and Cursor

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Snapchat revealed on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
  • The organization is introducing Easy Lens CLI, which builds on its existing Easy Lens tool, which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on the web and mobile.
  • Recent findings suggest that the launch indicates that Snapchat is looking to lower the barrier to creating AR content, while making its platform more accessible to developers who are increasingly using AI coding assistants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Snapchat revealed on Wednesday that it’s giving Lens creators the ability to build Lenses using the AI coding assistants they already use, like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Snapchat Lenses, which are a core part of the social network’s platform, are AR effects that let users alter their appearance, add digital objects to their surroundings, or interact with animated experiences through the camera.

The organization is introducing Easy Lens CLI, which builds on its existing Easy Lens tool, which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on the web and mobile. Easy Lens CLI brings that same idea into developers’ existing workflows, allowing AI assistants to handle the technical work while creators focus on the vision for the Lens itself.

Recent findings suggest that the launch indicates that Snapchat is looking to lower the barrier to creating AR content, while making its platform more accessible to developers who are increasingly using AI coding assistants. Instead of requiring creators to learn how to use Snapchat’s own development tools, the company is bringing Lens creation into the AI coding workflows they already use, which could in turn expand the pool of people who build for Snapchat.

In a recent development, developers enrolled in Snapchat’s Lens+ Payouts program can earn from the Lenses they create with Easy Lens CLI. Snapchat notes it paid out $1.8 million to Lens+ community creators last month.

Sources indicate that lens creators can describe the Lens they want in plain language, and their AI assistant handles the process from start to finish, Snapchat says. That includes building with more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, generating previews, and publishing them to Snapchat and tracking their performance.

With Easy Lens CLI, Snapchat notes developers can create everything from Web Lens games with leaderboards to camera effects and beauty filters.

AI assistants can generate assets, build and test Lenses, address errors, and send updated versions directly to the creator’s phone. The new capability can take a game from an initial idea to a published Lens in a single day, without developers having to write code themselves, Snapchat says.

The tool is aimed at different types of creators. The organization notes that game developers can bring existing browser games to Snapchat as Web Lenses, while AI creators can use assets from their preferred tools to build Lenses in their own style. Additionally, agencies and brands can turn existing campaign videos, images, and other brand assets into AR experiences with less production time.

Easy Lens CLI runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux.

Tech lawsuits defined 2026 — and lawmakers want more

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.
  • Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.
  • With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass latest protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block consumers from filing lawsuits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.

Congress is scrambling to provide legal recourse for deepfakes and online grooming.

With just a few weeks remaining, lawmakers are trying to pass latest protections for victims of online harm before the end of 2026, targeting deepfake creators and online platforms that block consumers from filing lawsuits.

Sources indicate that on Tuesday, members of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hosted a hearing calling for the end of forced arbitration for online harms. Their immediate target was Roblox, which they accused of evading legal complaints about children allegedly groomed on the platform by enforcing its own forced arbitration clause against customers who agreed to the terms as minors, in some cases even under the age of 10. Separately, a few blocks away, Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-NY) and Laurel Lee (R-FL) brought hotel heiress Paris Hilton to Capitol Hill to advocate for the Defiance Act, which would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators.

Industry observers note that “The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors,” Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), who chairs the Judiciary subcommittee, told reporters after the Roblox hearing. “The more I see these companies evade regulations, the more I think there is nothing as powerful as a jury.” Hawley introduced a new bill with ranking member Dick Durbin (D-IL) to render arbitration agreements unenforceable for disputes over alleged child sexual exploitation or “child cyber injury,” which could include “reputational harm, mental suffering,” or death.

“The best thing we can do in terms of enforcement is we can open up the courthouse doors”.

Roblox has sought to enforce its arbitration clause in lawsuits it’s facing over allegations that owners were groomed on the gaming platform as minors, despite the company’s claims of protections. Roblox is facing about 180 lawsuits in a consolidated case over its alleged role in failing to protect children. Under the arbitration process, the public would not get to see legal discovery like the kind that’s come to light under recent cases against Meta. Hawley called the jury system “corruption-proof” and “an incredibly big hammer.”.

Roblox has denied that it’s trying to dodge accountability. “Safety has been central to Roblox since we rolled out. We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” Roblox’s global head of public policy Nicky Jackson Colaço remarked in a statement. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”.

Congress has only a little more than three more weeks left in session before the end of the year, and a fresh Democratic majority will be sworn in come January. Republicans are expected to do their best to push through President Donald Trump’s nominees for judgeships and executive branch posts like FCC commissioner in the lame-duck session, as well as try to pass year-end bills like the National Defense Authorization Act, which often includes a range of other policy items. But some lawmakers are holding out hope that they can open up courthouses to new litigation over deepfake abuse and child predation.

Recent findings suggest that litigation has become one of the more successful ways for survivors of online harm to seek change. Congress has failed to pass many prominent child safety, privacy, and consumer protection bills, though it has begun to tackle the deepfake issue through the Take It Down Act. At the same time, attorneys general and individual plaintiffs have collected significant settlements and legal wins despite the broad scope of tech’s legal shield, Section 230. If bills like the Defiance Act or those seeking to end forced arbitration were to pass, tech companies and perpetrators of online harms could become vulnerable to a newly introduced wave of legal challenges.

“You will be amazed by how quickly the tech giant will change its behavior once it is sued in public court”.

According to recent reports, in addition to Hawley and Durbin’s bill about forced arbitration, Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Katie Britt (R-AL), and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced a similar bill with a slightly different approach, including explicitly covering data privacy violations. At the Roblox hearing, Northwestern University law professor Myriam Gilles, an expert on forced arbitration, noted she’s testified before Congress many times on this topic, but “never expected to come before this body to talk about its use against 9 year olds.” Passing either proposal, she said, would have a profound impact. “You will be amazed by how rapidly the manufacturer will change its behavior once it is sued in public court.”.

According to recent reports, the Defiance Act would let victims of nonconsensual intimate deepfakes sue their creators for damages, in an attempt to raise the cost of creating these kinds of images. Hilton visited Washington earlier this year to share how an intimate non-deepfake video of her at age 19 shared without her consent impacted her life, and she used her story to advocate for the Defiance Act. At Tuesday’s press conference, she remarked she would come back to Congress as many times as necessary for the bill to become law. “Some people might have thought that was the end of my fight,” Hilton said. “But when I make a promise to survivors, I keep it.”.

It has been revealed that hilton said over 50 million people have been victimized by sexually explicit deepfakes. “For me personally, strangers have created over 100,000 AI-generated explicit images and videos portraying me in the most graphic and disturbing ways imaginable,” Hilton said. “If this can happen to someone with my resources and my platform, imagine how powerless a young girl might feel facing this completely alone.”.

Hilton’s comments were followed by Elliston Berry, an advocate who mentioned a classmate made an explicit deepfake image of her friend group “from an innocent social media post” when she was 14, and distributed it throughout her school. “In a matter of seconds, my sense of security disappeared,” she said. “For me, the Defiance Act means recognition that victims deserve to be heard, that their experience matters, and that their right to seek justice should not depend on how rapidly technology advances.”.

Workers now treat jobs like portfolios as AI hiring erodes trust

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Survey data from thousands of professionals shows why many treat a second paycheck as unemployment insurance.
  • Ask a growing number of professionals about a second job, and many call it unemployment insurance.
  • According to recent reports, hiring data explains why.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Survey data from thousands of professionals shows why many treat a second paycheck as unemployment insurance.

Ask a growing number of professionals about a second job, and many call it unemployment insurance. In an Enhancv survey of 1,000 professionals holding multiple full-time roles, 79.5% agreed a second paycheck protects them against layoffs and economic instability.

According to recent reports, hiring data explains why. According to a survey of 1,066 U.S. job seekers, 50.5% received a rejection with no human feedback in the past year. Workers once traded loyalty for job security, but many professionals now manage employment like a financial portfolio. In other words, they rely on income from several jobs so that losing one job doesn’t wipe out their earnings.

Hiring decisions now happen out of view. Among the 538 respondents who got silent rejections, 63.8% believed an algorithm made the call. Younger applicants experience silence more often than older ones. Silent rejections reached 62.2% of applicants aged 25 to 34 and 61.5% of those aged 18 to 24, compared with 32% of those 55 and older.

It has been revealed that employers rarely disclosed AI use, according to 68.5% of candidates. Among respondents, 31.4% abandoned an application after a one-way video or chatbot screen, and nearly half of respondents (47.7%) agreed that AI hiring tools are biased against their age, race, gender, or background. Candidates also use AI, with 49.6% admitting they relied on it.

In a recent development, some job postings never lead to hire, and workers call them ghost listings. Enhancv surveyed another 1,000 US professionals in March 2026. Among respondents with eight or more years of experience, 51% had encountered ghost listings, which are postings for roles the employer never intended to fill. Among 411 senior respondents, 31% said employers asked for strategy decks or marketing intelligence before making an offer.

In a recent development, overall, 37% of respondents reported direct out-of-pocket losses. A job listing with no actual opening still costs applicants hours and money. In addition, 16.1% saw a role reposted as fresh right after a rejection email. Senior candidates who hand over strategy decks or marketing ideas before an offer may be giving away work for a job that doesn’t exist.

Sources indicate that enhancv survey of 1,000 professionals with multiple full-time jobs also asked what it would take to give up the second paycheck. About half said they would need a 21% to 50% raise to give up the second paycheck. Another 12.9% said they would not leave, no matter the pay.

Enhancv’s data shows that overemployment spans office-based and hybrid roles across many industries. About 50.4% of respondents work mostly in the office and 26.5% work hybrid, so 76.9% have at least some on-site time. By industry, education leads at 16.6%, ahead of operations at 12.9% and healthcare at 11%. Software engineers account for just 2.3%, so most people hold multiple full-time jobs outside tech.

AI makes holding two jobs easier. In the same survey, 28% report a significant drop in workload from AI tools, and 8% noted it fell by more than half. One in four meets primary targets in 30 hours or less. Roughly 26.4% rely on speed alone to keep multiple jobs running. Calendar blocking helps 15% of respondents, and 14.5% carry separate devices.

AI tools let workers finish tasks faster, but many employers still measure and reward hours worked. Many workers respond by adding a second job, so no single employer controls their income. Return-to-office mandates add to the distrust. An Enhancv return-to-office survey of 1,000 US employees found that 72% see the rules as a way to force resignations. Separately, 36% started a side hustle after their employer announced a return-to-work mandate.

Sources indicate that workers have learned that a job can disappear without warning, and that a rejection can arrive without reason. Enhancv’s research shows many now play around both.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Best Buy is selling Blu-rays directly through its website and in physical stores again after exiting Blu-ray and DVD sales in 2023.
  • Recent findings suggest that the Best Buy website’s movie section presently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” New titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025).
  • Industry observers note that most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Best Buy is selling Blu-rays directly through its website and in physical stores again after exiting Blu-ray and DVD sales in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that the Best Buy website’s movie section presently lists 15 Blu-rays (including one two-pack) that are “sold & shipped by Best Buy.” New titles available include The Odyssey (2026), Project Hail Mary (2026), Supergirl (2026), Super Mario Galaxy (2026), and Obsession (2025). Best Buy is also selling some older titles on Blu-ray, including It’s a Wonderful Life (1943), Saving Private Ryan (1998), and The Godfather (1972).

Industry observers note that most of the Blu-rays are available for purchase online and can be delivered to an address or picked up at a Best Buy store within a few days. As of this writing, The Odyssey appears to be in stock at Best Buy stores, as it’s presently listed as available for pickup within as little as an hour.

Ars Technica reached out to Best Buy to ask whether customers can expect the store to continue selling Blu-rays moving forward.

In October 2023, Best Buy revealed that it would stop selling Blu-rays and DVDs online and in stores starting in 2024.

“To state the obvious, the way we watch movies and TV highlights is much different today than it was decades ago. Making this change gives us more space and opportunity to bring customers new and innovative tech for them to explore, discover and enjoy,” a Best Buy spokesperson said in a statement issued at the time.

Last year, the Best Buy website started selling Blu-rays and DVDs from third parties via its online marketplace.

Numerous other companies have reduced or ended their Blu-ray and/or DVD businesses in recent years. Target, for instance, only sells the discs in stores during special occasions (like holidays or for big releases) now. Disney outsourced its DVD and Blu-ray business to Sony, which subsequently stopped selling recordable Blu-rays to people, and DVD rental company Redbox went out of business.

That mentioned, physical media, including Blu-rays and DVDs, still have a place in many people’s homes. Because digital copies of movies and indicates can be plucked from online platforms and people’s libraries that were previously “purchased” (but truly only rented) without warning, enthusiasts continue relying on physical media. Enthusiasts also opt for physical copies of movies and shows for better picture and/or sound quality than what’s available digitally, as well as for bragging rights.

Overall, the sales of Blu-rays and DVDs in the US have been steadily declining, and annual consumer spending dropped 9.3 percent from 2024 to 2025, according to the Digital Entertainment Group (DEG). During this same time, however, consumer spending on 4K Blu-ray discs specifically increased 12 percent year over year, per DEG.

A resurgence in Blu-ray sales has been associated with the growth of collectible SteelBooks, which are Blu-rays sold in collectible steel boxes, and Gen Z, which, in some cases, are even turning to video rental stores for Blu-rays and DVDs.

“We’re seeing a lot of evidence, including at the Criterion Mobile Closet, that more young people are thinking about physical media in a different way,” Peter Becker, president of Criterion, which sells Blu-rays and DVDs online, told the Los Angeles Times in February. “In an age where so much is available to us on demand, it becomes increasingly notable to us.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been a wild ride for Google Pixel’s App Lock feature, but the tech giant is officially re-releasing the feature today, right alongside its debut on Samsung Galaxy devices.
  • App Lock debuted on Google Pixel in an August build of Android 17 QPR2’s beta.
  • The feature is still only in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 for Google Pixel devices, an upgrade that should be released to the stable track in early 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been a wild ride for Google Pixel’s App Lock feature, but the tech giant is officially re-releasing the feature today, right alongside its debut on Samsung Galaxy devices.

App Lock debuted on Google Pixel in an August build of Android 17 QPR2’s beta. The feature lets customers hide apps behind a biometric or PIN authentication layer while also hiding notifications, widgets, and data from AI services. It’s a useful privacy features, but one that Google removed in subsequent updates. The feature later returned in QPR3 Beta 3 last month, and today Google is officially re-releasing it.

The feature is still only in Android 17 QPR3 Beta 3 for Google Pixel devices, an upgrade that should be released to the stable track in early 2027.

You can still access App Lock by long-pressing on an app icon and adding it to the app lock list.

In a post on Reddit, Google’s Community Engagement Manager details that App Lock on Google Pixel was removed for improvements before getting a full release:.

…the product team decided to temporarily pull back the feature from the QPR2 Beta to allow for additional polish, thorough testing, and robust integration across all system surfaces.

That’s why Samsung’s One UI 9.5 beta release today also brings support for App Lock. The feature is built into Android 17 QPR2, seemingly the release that One UI 9.5 is based on, but Google Pixel devices aren’t getting it until QPR3. As far as release timelines go, this means that Samsung’s Galaxy S27 series will probably ship with this feature out of the box, where Pixel phones won’t get it until around March or so. One UI 9.5 won’t roll out for older Galaxy devices until May, if One UI 8.5 serves as an example.

The future of tech will not be inclusive by default

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1178 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ten years ago, QueerTech began with a feeling that too many 2SLGBTQI+ people in the technology sector know well: not belonging.
  • My co-founder Andy Saldaña and I were working at different companies in tech and kept running into the same frustration.
  • Industry observers note that I grew up in Morocco, where being queer was, and continues to be, illegal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ten years ago, QueerTech began with a feeling that too many 2SLGBTQI+ people in the technology sector know well: not belonging.

My co-founder Andy Saldaña and I were working at different companies in tech and kept running into the same frustration. We could see the possibility of the sector around us, had the skills to succeed, and believed technology, when stewarded responsibly, could change lives. Yet we could not see a place for ourselves, as queer professionals, within it.

Industry observers note that I grew up in Morocco, where being queer was, and continues to be, illegal. In 2007, I left for Fresh York City in pursuit of the "American Dream." There, I quickly realized this dream was based on a contradiction — opportunity without equal rights. Finally, I moved to Montreal, drawn to Canada’s reputation for respecting people across cultures, religions, and identities.

Across this journey, I expected geography to change my sense of belonging. It never did. So in 2016, Andy and I started small. QueerTech was a volunteer-run community group built around a simple need: to find one another, create connections, and make space for queer people in an industry where many of us felt invisible.

Recent findings suggest that today, QueerTech is a national nonprofit working across workforce development, entrepreneurship, research, responsible technology, and community. Our scale has changed, but the need has not. What has evolved is our understanding of what meaningful inclusion requires: not only creating spaces where queer people belong, but breaking down the systemic barriers that determine who gets access to opportunities, who advances into leadership, and who has the power to shape the future of technology.

The scope of our mission, spanning inclusive technology and professional wellbeing, demands ambitious goals and innovative programming grounded in collaboration and practical impact. Our community-first approach supports 2SLGBTQI+ professionals from industry entry through career advancement and entrepreneurship, while driving systemic change through partnerships with industry, investors, regulators, and community organizations.

QueerTech’s goals for the Canadian tech ecosystem are:.

Increasing 2SLGBTQI+ representation to 20 percent across the sector.

Advancing 2SLGBTQI+ leadership representation to 5 percent.

Increasing funding for 2SLGBTQI+-owned ventures to 15 percent of total invested capital.

QT Access: Building pathways into tech through skills development, mentorship and career preparation.

QT Leaders: Advancing professionals into decision-making roles that shape workplace culture, policy and innovation.

QT Founders: Equipping queer entrepreneurs with tools, networks and access to capital.

QT Events: Creating safer spaces for connection, learning and opportunity, both in-person and online.

Our responsible technology priorities center on the QT Inclusive AI Initiative. Launched in 2026, it combines self-assessment tools, inclusive AI training, national research, community dialogue, practical governance frameworks and cross-sector partnerships to strengthen AI literacy, accountability, inclusive practices, and collaboration.

Sources indicate that these efforts are grounded in a growing body of evidence about the barriers 2SLGBTQI+ professionals face, both within the technology sector and through the systems it creates. QueerTech’s 2026 research makes the scale of those challenges difficult to ignore.

Industry observers note that queerTech’s national Industry Census found 2SLGBTQI+ tech workers reported harassment and discrimination at roughly twice the rate of their non-2SLGBTQI+ peers: 44 percent reported harassment and 50 percent discrimination. Another 35 percent reported bias from AI hiring tools (versus 22 percent of peers). Inclusion in technology can no longer be measured only by who works inside the industry. We must also examine the systems the industry builds and deploys, including who participates in decisions, whose perspectives influence innovation, and who benefits from these advanced technologies.

Industry observers note that this year, QueerTech studied both sides of that equation. Our research into AI development found 43 percent of Canadian technology companies reported limited to no formal processes for addressing bias, while 71 percent reported limited to no organizational support for equitable representation.

It has been revealed that our research into AI use in human resources also exposed a significant disconnect between institutional perceptions and queer professionals’ experiences. While 86 percent of HR professionals believed 2SLGBTQI+ employees were "comfortable being out," our 2026 Census found only 37 percent of queer professionals were "out" at work to a great extent — a disparity of nearly 50 percent.

According to recent reports, the cost of that disconnect is higher than any one workplace. When queer professionals are overlooked, stalled or pushed out, companies lose skill, experience, and perspective. When people most likely to encounter bias are missing from product decisions, preventable blind spots can become features of automated systems and travel farther, faster and with less visibility.

In a recent development, that is not just an inclusion problem. It is a talent, product, and competitiveness problem for Canada’s innovation economy. As Canada invests in its technological future and digital sovereignty, we cannot afford to overlook talent, limit leadership access, or build technologies that fail to serve the people who depend on them.

The next question is what the sector does with that evidence.

In a recent development, on Nov. 18 and 19, more than 700 tech professionals will gather in Toronto for the 2026 QT Qonference (QTQ) under the theme Who Gets to Trust AI? This question is critical, given that trust in technology is shaped by various decentralized, and often competing, entities across the entire ecosystem. Developers build the systems. Employers decide how they are used. Executives set priorities. Policymakers create the rules. Workers and communities experience the results.

QTQ convenes these groups to address the same challenges from different perspectives. Better decisions happen when the people building, governing, and using technology are at the same table, but participation alone is not enough. Meaningful change requires institutions to translate conversation into action: removing barriers to opportunity, embedding accountability into technology development and deployment, and giving affected communities a meaningful role in shaping these technologies.

Recent findings suggest that the future of tech will not be inclusive by default. It will be shaped by who is included in the decisions that define it. The responsibility belongs to all of us — industry leaders, investors, policymakers, and communities — to ensure that innovation expands opportunity rather than reinforces existing inequalities. Inclusion is not a concession to innovation; it’s a condition for responsible, sustainable innovation.

This article represents the opinion of its writer.

Industry observers note that queerTech is a national nonprofit advancing 2SLGBTQI+ talent, entrepreneurship, and inclusive technology across Canada’s tech ecosystem. Through community-led programming, original research, strategic partnerships, and actionable inclusion tools, QueerTech builds pathways to opportunity for queer professionals, leaders, and entrepreneurs while working with ecosystem partners to address the institutional barriers that limit access, advancement, and participation. Guided by its Vision 2034, QueerTech is working toward a technology ecosystem where queer people don't just participate — they thrive, lead, and help shape the future of innovation.

Breaking: Sam Altman indicates his life is so weird that he’s unfazed by Andrew Garfield portraying him in upcoming movie

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hollywood has found plenty of material and cinematic inspiration from a string of Silicon Valley scandals and power struggles in recent years.
  • “You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, smashed box office expectations, and Netflix’s limited series “The Altruists” comes out Thursday to tell the story of Sam Bankman-Fried and the downfall of FTX.
  • As the founder and CEO of OpenAI, one of the most influential companies of the century, Sam Altman isn’t going to escape the Hollywood treatment, either.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hollywood has found plenty of material and cinematic inspiration from a string of Silicon Valley scandals and power struggles in recent years.

“You Can See Everything,” the documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, smashed box office expectations, and Netflix’s limited series “The Altruists” comes out Thursday to tell the story of Sam Bankman-Fried and the downfall of FTX.

As the founder and CEO of OpenAI, one of the most influential companies of the century, Sam Altman isn’t going to escape the Hollywood treatment, either.

In “Artificial,” a biographical comedy-drama opening in theaters on Christmas, the lauded actor Andrew Garfield will portray Altman in a film that chronicles OpenAI’s rise and the internal turmoil that erupted when he was briefly ousted in 2023.

Sources indicate that “If you had told me 20 years ago that someone was going to make a movie about me, I think that would have struck me as … that would have been a very weird thing,” Altman said onstage at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday. “Now it doesn’t feel like it’s in like the top 10 weirdest things about my life.”.

Industry observers note that garfield is best known for his role as Spider-Man, but his massive break came in 2010, when he played Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin in “The Social Network” alongside Jesse Eisenberg as Mark Zuckerberg. (That film also had a sequel of sorts this year called “The Social Reckoning,” but it bombed at the box office.).

So, if Altman isn’t fazed by the looming release of “Artificial,” what’s actually the weirdest thing in his life?

“The fact that we are ushering in this technology that we have all of these very real concerns about, and that we have, we find ourselves in a role of such significance and such responsibility to make that go well,” Altman stated. “That’s a crazy situation to find yourself in.”.

Sure, that is pretty weird, Sam. It’s also weird that you use ChatGPT for parenting advice and don’t respect olive oil. But I’d wager to say it’s even weirder that there’s an upcoming film about the time your colleagues briefly ousted you because they were concerned that you can’t be trusted.

Say what you want about Mark Zuckerberg (I certainly have), but at least he’s honest about what he thinks about “The Social Network.”.

According to recent reports, “It was weird, man,” Zuckerberg reflected on a podcast last year. “They got all these very specific details of what I was wearing, or these specific things correct, but then the whole narrative arc around my motivations and all this stuff were like, completely wrong … The whole arc is like, I’m somehow motivated by trying to find a girlfriend, [but] I was dating Priscilla [Chan] before I started Facebook.”.

Zuckerberg stated he knew his employees would be tempted to see the movie, so he organized a firm outing when it was released, even though the film hardly paints a flattering portrait of him.

Zuckerberg even had enough of a sense of humor to buy a prop from the film at auction. He owns an Ardsley High School T-shirt that Eisenberg wore in the movie and even wore it himself in a video with YouTubers Colin and Samir.

Eisenberg hasn’t been particularly complimentary of Zuckerberg, saying that he doesn’t want to think of himself as “associated with somebody like that.” And while “Artificial” hasn’t hit theaters yet, Garfield doesn’t seem to have a much more favorable opinion of the tech founder he portrays.

In a recent development, “I don’t know Sam Altman. I’ve never met him,” Garfield told Esquire. “But I think anyone who takes on that level of responsibility for a company or technology that you know is going to do a hell of a lot of damage to the soul of humanity [must have] a certain ability to dissociate.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a newly introduced interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month.
  • Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.
  • In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue remarked Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a newly introduced interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue remarked Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:.

In a recent development, we were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:.

Industry observers note that when we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:.

Sources indicate that the really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe noted “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very vital to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a new logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe said he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:.

Recent findings suggest that we could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The issue of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:.

Well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a tech giant and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift….

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This settles a lawsuit that goes all the way back to 2021.
  • Industry observers note that siriusXM has agreed to provide podcast transcripts for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community, as part of a legal settlement that resolves a lawsuit from 2021.
  • Industry observers note that this won't be a slapdash affair.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This settles a lawsuit that goes all the way back to 2021.

Industry observers note that siriusXM has agreed to provide podcast transcripts for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community, as part of a legal settlement that resolves a lawsuit from 2021. The settlement impacts both SiriusXM and Pandora podcasts.

Industry observers note that this won't be a slapdash affair. The transcripts must include speaker identification, any relevant atmospherics, sound effects, proper punctuation, paragraph breaks and just about everything else one would need to properly enjoy the content. The decree also requires human cleanup, so an actual person will have to review the transcripts if assisted by speech recognition algorithms.

The company will build custom data dictionaries of words and phrases specific to each podcast and develop an active style guide with input from the suit's plaintiffs. Finally, it must train staff on Deaf culture and communication access. All in all, this looks like a solid win for accessibility advocates.

Sources indicate that "Podcasts have become a huge part of how we share news, ideas, stories and information, and deaf people deserve equal access to all of it," said plaintiff James Munro. "We hope this sparks even more change across the podcasting world. Let's make inaccessible podcasts a thing of the past!".

The original lawsuit was filed back in 2021. At that time, neither SiriusXM or Pandora offered podcast transcripts of any kind for the deaf and hard-of-hearing community. This was seen as a violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act.

Sources indicate that there are still podcast platforms out there without robust transcription systems in place. Nick Kiego, CEO of the National Association of the Deaf, mentioned that he hopes "this settlement will serve as a benchmark for other providers of podcast entertainment, opening the doors for deaf and hard of hearing people to fully access, engage in and enjoy the latest conversations in everything from politics to pop culture.".

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It looks comparatively cheap — and that might be a good thing in this economy.

It looks comparatively cheap — and that might be a good thing in this economy.

It has been revealed that for a while there, it seemed like Lenovo had given up on selling handheld gaming PCs, hiking the price of its Legion Go 2 and Legion Go S far higher than other RAM-starved competitors. A decent one can easily cost $1,000 if not $2,000 now. But it looks like Lenovo might be about to announce a relatively cheap handheld once again— the Legion Go Beam.

According to recent reports, windows Latest has leaked images of the handheld, and there’s no question it’s designed to be a value alternative to even the manufacturer’s least expensive Legion Go S variant. While it’s got the same significant stippled grips and triggers for comfort, there’s only one USB-C port on the top instead of two, a comparatively cheap-looking D-pad, no touchpad, and only a single tiny intake and exhaust for its fan.

Industry observers note that there’s no SteamOS logo where that would go, so it likely runs Windows instead… but then there’s that name, “Beam.” Perhaps you’ll “beam” your games to it because it’s a streaming and cloud gaming handheld, instead of one that primarily plays games on its own chip? Maybe that’s why it doesn’t need as much airflow as previous handhelds?

Perhaps there’s a partnership with Xbox Cloud Gaming specifically, and that’s why it’s all lit up in Xbox green?

According to recent reports, but it might just be green because it looks nice with white, which has been the “value” color for handhelds so far (see: ROG Ally, Xbox Ally, and the Windows-based Legion Go S). And it might be “Beam” because there’s a literal beam of light on the bottom, even though the first thing I do with most handhelds is turn any and all distracting RGB lighting off. Or maybe it’s “Beam” just because it sounds like a friendly, fun, value-oriented name, instead of something “S” or “Pro.”.

It has been revealed that I won’t begin to speculate on the Legion Go Beam’s price, except to say that “cheap” may be relative. The Legion Go S was originally supposed to cost $499, but wound up costing far more except on the occasional sale. The Legion Go 2 was supposed to start at $1,099 but wound up costing $1,500 and up after RAMageddon. Streaming-first handhelds have been far cheaper, though, like the $249 Sony PlayStation Portal.

Lenovo has a history of announcing its newly introduced gaming devices at CES in January each year, including previous Legion Go handhelds, so I’m expecting to see an official announcement of the Lenovo Legion Go Beam then. Even if so, that doesn’t mean it’ll be available in January — there’s often a many-month lag.

Motorola Razr Fold finally gets its Android 17 patch – hopefully the next 7 years go faster

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Motorola Razr Fold introduced with Android 16 back in May 2026, and it remains a really good option for those looking to pick up a book-style foldable in the US.
  • But nowhere was it promises that Motorola would speed things up at all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Motorola has kicked off its Android 17 rollout for the Razr Fold, marking the first major patch for the organization’s first book-style foldable, and the start of a potentially interest 7 years of software support.

The Motorola Razr Fold introduced with Android 16 back in May 2026, and it remains a really good option for those looking to pick up a book-style foldable in the US. On top of solid specs across the board, it also carries the promise of 7 years of software support, something that few other Moto devices can tout.

But nowhere was it promises that Motorola would speed things up at all. A little over 3 months after Motorola announced the update and several weeks after other Motorola devices were updated to Android 17, the Motorola Razr Fold is finally getting its own Android 17 update.

Rolling out now, Android 17 for the Razr Fold is a 4.15GB~ patch that appears to be available at least somewhat broadly. Reports are popping up on Reddit including one report from the EU (Hungary, specifically), with another user apparently in a Spanish-speaking region also seeing the update.

We’re still waiting to see if the enhancement is available in the US (there’s a backlog of updates on our unit), but it’s certainly an update to look forward to. Apparently, Motorola finally fixed a weird UI matter that affected the Telegram app, something we ran into when using the device earlier this year.

Recent findings suggest that it’s great to see the update out, but it’s noteworthy that Motorola is not setting a particularly encouraging precedent here. Razr Fold is one of the company’s first devices to be promised 7 years of OS updates and software support, and its flagship-tier status certainly would have most expecting it to be updated ahead of some of Motorola’s more affordable, lower-tier devices that were updated over a month ago. Whatever the case, hopefully Motorola will speed things up over the next few years, especially with its $1,600 flagship Signature 27 on the horizon with the same software promises.

According to recent reports, microsoft told its Ignite conference that businesses choose Copilot over Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT because it is cheaper to run, citing a study it commissioned from GigaOm. Anthropic says non-coding Claude Enterprise consumers spend under $75 a month, well below the study’s $205 figure.

Microsoft says companies are choosing its Copilot AI assistant over Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT because it costs less to run, Bloomberg reported. Judson Althoff, who runs Microsoft’s commercial business, made the pitch at the organization’s Ignite conference on Tuesday. Microsoft has coached its salespeople to pitch Copilot against both rivals since July.

“Anything you can do in Claude or ChatGPT, you can do better with Copilot, and for less,” Althoff noted.

The claim leans on a study Microsoft paid research firm GigaOm to run, which found people would spend much less on Copilot. That study cited $205 a month per user for basic work. Anthropic notes its non-coding Claude Enterprise users spend under $75 a month on average.

It has been revealed that AI bills have become a massive worry for companies this year, with many capping staff AI use. Copilot offers a flat monthly fee for basic tasks, or pay-as-you-go pricing for heavier work. Microsoft itself cut back Claude Code licences for its own engineers in May over token costs.

In a recent development, copilot had more than 30 million paid users in June, a small share of the 450 million business users of Microsoft’s office software. Its daily users grew fivefold in a year, Microsoft said last month. AT&T pays for tens of thousands of staff to use it, though it also uses OpenAI’s Codex.

The fight is getting personal. Last week Anthropic added Claude Sheets and other office tools aimed at Excel. Microsoft’s Jacob Andreou stated at Ignite that rivals’ “simplified viewers and editors force compromise on power and collaboration.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey thinks Nvidia’s board is giving China exactly what it wants by removing the company’s longtime CEO and co-founder, Jensen Huang.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia, the leading semiconductor designer whose chips power much of the AI industry, is undergoing a critical, unexpected leadership change. Huang, who led the company for 33 years, stepped down last week amid several controversies, including his extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy who has been investigated for possibly smuggling Nvidia chips into China to circumvent U.S. export restrictions.

“China wants Jensen out, so I want him in,” Luckey mentioned onstage at The Upcoming York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, repeating a statement he posted on X last week. “They’re thrilled to have Jensen out… There’s a reason it’s knocking a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market cap. They know it makes America weaker to knock him out.”.

According to recent reports, luckey disagrees with Huang’s longstanding position that Nvidia should have more leeway to export chips to China. But he also recognizes that China stands to benefit if its domestic chipmakers can challenge Nvidia’s dominance.

According to recent reports, “China doesn’t want Nvidia to sell GPUs to Chinese companies,” Luckey stated. “There are Chinese companies that want to buy Nvidia GPUs… China will not give them an import permit because they want to build an internal domestic processor industry… not build one that is dependent on the United States.”.

Nvidia has stated as much itself — the U.S. government granted the company license to ship some of its powerful H200 chips to certain Chinese customers, but those sales were restricted by the Chinese government. Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress said during the company’s quarterly earnings call on Tuesday that it will no longer sell H200 chips in China at all.

Luckey is far from alone among industry peers in his defense of Huang.

It has been revealed that more than 200,000 people — including Elon Musk and the CEOs of Y Combinator, Databricks, Epic Games, Shopify, and Replit — have signed a petition calling for Nvidia to reinstate its founder. But Nvidia executives said during the tech giant’s earnings call on Tuesday that the company does not have looks to reappoint Huang, even though the founder offered to return.

#1518. Why GTA 6 doesn't have a 60 fps performance mode

Why GTA 6 doesn't have a 60 fps performance mode

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (836 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The biggest game of the year is only coming to consoles at launch.
  • Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is the most anticipated video game of all time.
  • There's no getting around it: GTA 6 may be the most important code in a box in the history of the medium.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest game of the year is only coming to consoles at launch.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6 is the most anticipated video game of all time. And it ain't close. I'll age myself hideously here, but the only handful of titles that have touched the same level of gaming hype in my four decades on this rock are Super Mario 64 (1996), the original Metal Gear Solid (1998), and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (also 1998).

There's no getting around it: GTA 6 may be the most important code in a box in the history of the medium. Oh, and if you're wondering, here's how long it will take you to download GTA 6. R.I.P. physical media. Unlike Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, there's no 60 frames per second (fps) mode in Rockstar's Vice City future mega hit.

Industry observers note that 60 fps is sadly off the table for the Leonida-set sandbox. I feel your pain. Rockstar recently confirmed GTA 6 is targeting 30 fps across consoles. At the time of pre-release writing, if the budget-focused Xbox Series S can hit that framerate reliably, I'll be extremely impressed.

It has been revealed that this frame rate target is entirely in keeping with Rockstar's history. The iconic developer has never released a console game at launch that hit more than 30 fps, with one exception. The criminally forgotten, quietly excellent Rockstar Games Presents Table Tennis, back in 2006. PC ports of GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 could obviously exceed 60 fps with powerful enough hardware thrown at them — and plenty of post-launch patches. Yet in the console space, Rockstar has generally kept within 30 fps (again, at launch).

GTA 6 is a definite outlier for this console generation in terms of performance. On PS5 and Xbox Series X, many big-budget games offer 60 fps performance modes. Grand Theft Auto is probably the only video game franchise big enough to buck this frame-rate trend and get away with it.

What will 30 fps look like vs 60 fps in GTA 6? The simple answer is added input lag. I'm crossing my digits that the frame pacing of the biggest game of the generation will be consistent, which should hopefully provide a stable visual experience. Still, there's no question 60 fps normally feels vastly smoother than 30 fps gameplay.

It has been revealed that in terms of input lag — the delay you can physically feel while holding a controller — we're talking 16.7ms vs 33.3ms. There's a reason 60 fps has become the default standard for this console generation: it's way smoother to play. I'd happily take an upscaled 1080p or 1440p title at 60 fps over a full-fat 4K game running at 30 fps.

If you're lucky enough to own a PS5 Pro, GTA 6 should look a whole lot better thanks to Sony's second stab at PSSR upscaling (that's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution, if you're not up to speed on your techy acronyms). Regardless of input lag on any of the consoles, it would be surprising if a game with likely the biggest budget of all time didn't hit an unprecedented level of image quality across platforms. But if you want the best experience, PS5 Pro is where it's at.

As for the gameplay on Xbox Series X and the base PS5? They'll likely look excellent, too. And don't discount the Series S, either. Microsoft's little white box actually has a CPU that's broadly similar to the one you'll find in the Series X. Will there be cutbacks to the GTA 6 experience on Series S? Almost certainly. Expect reduced crowds, draw distances and traffic. Still, despite the obviously lower resolution compared to the PS5 Pro, the general gameplay experience should be mostly the same.

In a recent development, there are whispers of a surprisingly early PC port of GTA 6 in the opening months of 2027. If that dream scenario does occur, a combination of NVIDIA's DLSS 4.5 Multi Frame Generation and VRR tech could allow for a 4K/120 fps Vice City experience. At launch, though, the best PS5 and Xbox Series X players can hope for is around 1440p at 30 fps, due to the relative weakness of console CPUs compared to cutting-edge PC silicon.

Rockstar has got me, though. I'm totally going to double dip when the game eventually lands on PC. I'm lucky enough to have only slightly overpaid for my NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. If I sold it today — during these bleak AI data farm times — I'd triple my money on a card that should officially cost $1,9999. Paired with the current fastest gaming CPU on the market and 64GB of DDR5 RAM, my PC is the platform I ultimately want to experience GTA 6 on. I've been playing GTA 5: Enhanced Edition a lot lately at 4K/120 fps with all the ray-traced bells and whistles. I can't wait to do the same for its sequel.

Windows Server 2028 trades compatibility for out-of-the-box security

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its upcoming security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core.
  • Recent findings suggest that STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance.
  • The latest Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft’s Ignite announcements this week went beyond the Office-in-Copilot overhaul with the reveal of the Windows Server 2028 Public Preview and its upcoming security-by-default stance and what Microsoft calls Hardened Server Core. Windows Server 2028 will implement a default security framework that Microsoft claims is aligned with hardened DoD benchmarks, such as the Defense Information Systems Agency’s (DISA) Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG).

Recent findings suggest that STIGs work by providing a standard security framework for system administrators to follow recommended guidance. In the past, Windows Server admins were left to start from a blank canvas and then implement hardening configurations for operations. Secure baselines were available but not the default. Microsoft says that concern is now managed: “The secure configuration is the starting state, not a project you run after setup. That closes the window where a newly deployed server sits exposed while it waits to be hardened.”.

The latest Windows Server 2028 hardened-by-default state will only be available for the Server Core installs. Windows Server Desktop Experience installs do not include the changed stance.

It has been revealed that this isn’t to say that system administrators won’t still have the final say on which security protocols are activated, just that the default package now ships in a pre-hardened state. Kerberos is now the default over NTLM, with protections added to LSASS; TLS is automatically restricted to modern cipher suites; key exchange uses “hybrid post-quantum key exchange” based on the quantum-safe ML-KEM; and remote desktop authentication and PowerShell script block logging get stricter as well.

Recent findings suggest that microsoft’s native NVMe storage stack was originally introduced via an enhancement to Windows Server 2025, but it required administrators to enable it manually. The update eliminated NVMe translation through a SCSI stack while improving speeds and reducing overhead. The redesigned stack will now be default-on in Windows Server 2028.

Industry observers note that microsoft is upfront, noting that the upcoming hardened security settings may break things due to software compatibility challenges with older protocols, legacy authentication, or management tools and scripts. The tech giant encourages owners to try things and provide feedback about what goes wrong. “We want to hear where a hardened default gets in the way of a real workload: which setting, which application, and what you had to change to get it working,” the Windows Server Team said in a blog post. “That is how the defaults get better before general availability.”.

Microsoft suggests that people use the preview build as a test bed to determine where concerns like compatibility still arise. This is not a release candidate build and shouldn’t be treated as such. Despite the new security stance that comes with the preview build, hardware-backed protections like Secure Boot and DMA requirements won’t be enforced until a later preview build. Kerberos is now the default preference over NTLM, but NTLM blocking itself will still have to wait for a later preview release.

Beyond those limitations, the current build has a known issue that cuts into its hardened goals. According to the release notes, “A race condition in the TLS hybrid key exchange implementation may cause the LSASS service to crash when hybrid groups are negotiated by a TLS server.” Microsoft recommends disabling hybrid-key exchange groups until the problem is addressed.

System administrators and curious homelabbers interested in testing the newly introduced Windows Server 2028 can do so by registering with the Microsoft Windows Insider Program.
